knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(P:=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}\) and \(F:=P\circ g\). Because \(f\) is convex PLQ, \(P\) is single-valued, firmly nonexpansive, piecewise affine, and directionally differentiable. Hence \(F\) is locally Lipschitz and directionally differentiable at \(\bar x\), with \(F'(\bar x;d)=P'(g(\bar x);Dg(\bar x)d)\) for every \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Its Clarke generalized Jacobian obeys \(\partial_CF(\bar x)\subseteq\{A Dg(\bar x):A\in\partial_CP(g(\bar x))\}\). Thus the proximal primitive supplies the nonsmooth local piece and the smooth inner map supplies the transported direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composing a smooth map with a convex PLQ proximal primitive preserves local Lipschitzness and transports directions through the proximal map's piecewise-affine derivative.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Compositions

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(y\in Y\), define the resolvent-composite residual by \[R(y):=G\bigl(y,J_A(H(y))\bigr),\qquad J_A:=(I+A)^{-1}.\] Maximal monotonicity of \(A\) makes \(J_A:X\to X\) single-valued and firmly nonexpansive. Consequently, if \(G\) and \(H\) are locally Lipschitz, then \(R\) is locally Lipschitz. This representation includes residuals formed from a parameter-dependent point passed through a resolvent and then coupled to an outer equation map.

children.top_down_role: Interaction among smooth outer maps, nonsmooth primitives, and shared arguments.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested-Primitive Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive finite nesting of locally Lipschitz equation primitives over a common parameter space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q\ge 1\) and \(x\in X_0\). Define \[u_q(x):=Q_q(H_q(x)),\qquad u_i(x):=Q_i\bigl(H_i(x,u_{i+1}(x))\bigr)\quad(i=q-1,\ldots,1),\] and then define \[R(x):=G\bigl(x,u_1(x),\ldots,u_q(x)\bigr).\] This is a nested-primitive coupling. Under the stated local Lipschitz assumptions, every state map \(u_i:X_0\to X_i\) and the residual \(R:X_0\to W\) are locally Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested coupling recursively passes a common parameter and later primitive outputs through locally Lipschitz coupling maps, then inserts all resulting states into an outer residual.
assumptions_latex: \(X_0,\ldots,X_q\) and \(W\) are finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces, with \(q\ge 1\).
For each \(i=1,\ldots,q\), the primitive \(Q_i:X_i\to X_i\) is single-valued and locally Lipschitz.

The terminal coupling \(H_q:X_0\to X_q\), the couplings \(H_i:X_0\times X_{i+1}\to X_i\) for \(i=1,\ldots,q-1\), and the outer map \(G:X_0\times X_1\times\cdots\times X_q\to W\) are locally Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\) is a locally Lipschitz residual generated by recursively coupled nonsmooth primitives.

notation.meaning: single-valued locally Lipschitz primitive on X_i

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A block-structured residual map has the form \[R(z):=\bigl(R_1(z),\ldots,R_s(z)\bigr),\qquad z=(z_1,\ldots,z_s)\in Z,\] where a block \(R_i\) may depend on every component of \(z\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block residual stacks coupled component equations and preserves shared active selections when assembling local generalized Jacobian models.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonpolyhedral Normal-Cone Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local piecewise-polyhedral failure of convex normal-cone graphs in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), define \[N_C(x):=\begin{cases}\{v\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle v,z-x\rangle\le 0\ \text{for every }z\in C\},&x\in C,\\ \varnothing,&x\notin C.\end{cases}\] At a specified pair \((\bar x,\bar v)\in\operatorname{gph}N_C\), the normal-cone map is locally nonpolyhedral if there are no neighborhood \(U\) of \((\bar x,\bar v)\) and finitely many closed convex polyhedral sets \(P_1,\ldots,P_N\subset\mathbb{R}^{2n}\) such that \[\operatorname{gph}N_C\cap U=\left(\bigcup_{j=1}^{N}P_j\right)\cap U.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normal-cone map is locally nonpolyhedral at a graph pair when its graph cannot, in any neighborhood of that pair, be represented by finitely many closed convex polyhedral pieces.
assumptions_latex: \((\bar x,\bar v)\in\operatorname{gph}N_C\) is the graph pair at which local geometry is considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local nonpolyhedrality is precisely the failure of a finite piecewise-polyhedral representation of \(\operatorname{gph}N_C\) near \((\bar x,\bar v)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the positive dual cone by \[K^*:=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle y,z\rangle\ge 0\ \text{for every }z\in K\}.\] For \(x\in K\), the normal cone satisfies \(N_K(x)=(-K^*)\cap x^\perp\). Hence the conic generalized equation has the complementarity representation \[0\in F(x)+N_K(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in K,\quad F(x)\in K^*,\quad \langle x,F(x)\rangle=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic normal-cone equation is equivalent to primal cone feasibility, dual cone feasibility, and orthogonality of the primal and dual vectors.

children.title: Semismooth-Star Multifunctions
children.top_down_role: Coderivative-oriented semismoothness for generalized-equation models.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\) has locally closed graph near \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed estimate defines semismooth-star behavior of \(F\) at \((\bar x,\bar y)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limiting-coderivative definition in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The multifunction \(F\) is semismooth-star at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) if, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exists \(\delta>0\) such that every \((x,y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\) with \(\|(x,y)-(\bar x,\bar y)\|<\delta\), every \(y^*\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and every \(x^*\in D^*F(x,y)(y^*)\) satisfy \[\left|\langle x^*,x-\bar x\rangle-\langle y^*,y-\bar y\rangle\right|\le\varepsilon\,\|(x,y)-(\bar x,\bar y)\|\,\|(x^*,y^*)\|.\] The coderivative convention is \(x^*\in D^*F(x,y)(y^*)\) exactly when \((x^*,-y^*)\in N_{\operatorname{gph}F}(x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Semismooth-star behavior requires coderivative normals to become asymptotically orthogonal to displacements along the graph.
knowledge_statements.title: Semismooth-Star Multifunctions

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The B-subdifferential of \(F\) at \(\bar x\) is \[\partial_BF(\bar x):=\left\{A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}:\text{ there exist }x_k\in D_F,\ x_k\to\bar x,\ JF(x_k)\to A\right\}.\] Local Lipschitz continuity implies that \(F\) is differentiable almost everywhere and that nearby Jacobians are bounded; consequently, \(\partial_BF(\bar x)\) is nonempty and compact.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: B-subdifferential as a linear Newton approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semismoothness makes the B-subdifferential an ordinary or strong linear Newton approximation scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G:\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be Lipschitz continuous in a neighborhood of \(\bar x\in\Omega\). If \(G\) is semismooth at \(\bar x\), then \(\partial_B G\) defines a linear Newton approximation scheme for \(G\) at \(\bar x\). If \(G\) is strongly semismooth at \(\bar x\), then \(\partial_B G\) defines a strong linear Newton approximation scheme there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a reference point, the B-subdifferential of a Lipschitz semismooth map defines a linear Newton approximation scheme. Strong semismoothness gives a strong scheme.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limiting classical Jacobians of a locally Lipschitz mapping along differentiability points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G:\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), where \(\Omega\) is open, be locally Lipschitz at \(\bar x\in\Omega\). If \(N_G\) is the negligible set where \(G\) is not Fréchet differentiable, then
\[
\operatorname{Jac}G(\bar x)=\partial_B G(\bar x):=\left\{H\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}:\exists x^k\to\bar x,\ x^k\notin N_G,\ JG(x^k)\to H\right\}.
\]

children.title: Componentwise Jacobian Families
children.top_down_role: Generalized Jacobian constructions selected independently at the residual-component level.

knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Jacobian Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent assembly from scalar-component Bouligand gradient limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=(F_1,\ldots,F_m):U\subset\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be locally Lipschitz, and let \(D_i\) be the differentiability set of \(F_i\). Define the componentwise Bouligand gradient family by \[\partial_B^{\mathrm{cmp}}F(x):=\left\{A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}:A_{i:}\in\partial_BF_i(x)\text{ for every }i\right\},\qquad \partial_BF_i(x):=\left\{\lim_{k\to\infty}\nabla F_i(x_k):x_k\to x,\ x_k\in D_i\right\}.\] Rows may be generated by different sequences; hence this construction imposes no joint realizability condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The componentwise family contains every matrix obtained by independently choosing each row from the limiting gradients of the corresponding scalar component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial_B^{\mathrm{cmp}}F(x)=\prod_{i=1}^m\partial_BF_i(x)\) under rowwise identification.

notation.meaning: the i-th row of matrix A
Bouligand limiting-gradient set of component i

knowledge_statements.title: Rowwise Jacobian Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent assembly from row projections of the joint B-Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:U\subset\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be locally Lipschitz and differentiable on \(D_F\). For each row index define \[R_i(x):=\left\{a\in\mathbb R^{1\times n}:a=A_{i:}\text{ for some }A\in\partial_BF(x)\right\},\qquad \partial_BF(x):=\left\{\lim_{k\to\infty}JF(x_k):x_k\to x,\ x_k\in D_F\right\}.\] The rowwise Jacobian family is \[\mathcal R_F(x):=\left\{A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}:A_{i:}\in R_i(x)\text{ for all }i\right\}.\] Its rows need not originate from one common limiting Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project the joint B-Jacobian onto each row and then recombine those row projections independently; the resulting matrices form the rowwise family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial_BF(x)\subseteq\mathcal R_F(x)=\prod_{i=1}^mR_i(x)\).

notation.meaning: set where F is classically differentiable
i-th-row projection of the joint B-Jacobian

children.title: Cross-Row Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of row selections with a common nearby differentiability pattern.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Row Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common-sequence criterion for joint realizability of limiting rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For locally Lipschitz \(F:U\subset\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), a matrix \(A\in\mathcal R_F(x)\) is cross-row compatible at \(x\) precisely when there exists one sequence \((x_k)\subset D_F\) such that \[x_k\to x\quad\text{and}\quad JF(x_k)\to A.\] Equivalently, all rows satisfy \(\nabla F_i(x_k)\to A_{i:}\) along the same differentiability sequence. Thus cross-row compatibility is stronger than separate membership \(A_{i:}\in R_i(x)\), which may be witnessed by different sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A row assembly is compatible exactly when all its rows arise simultaneously along one sequence of points where the whole mapping is differentiable.
assumptions_latex: \(F:U\to\mathbb R^m\) is locally Lipschitz near \(x\in U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\text{ is cross-row compatible at }x\iff A\in\partial_BF(x)\).

children.title: Nonrealizable Matrix Assemblies
children.top_down_role: Assembled matrices that do not correspond to any coherent limiting Jacobian.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonrealizable Matrix Assemblies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A two-component map whose independently admissible rows cannot be jointly realized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(F:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^2\) by \(F(t)=(|t|,|t|)\). At \(0\), each row projection of \(\partial_BF(0)\) equals \(\{-1,1\}\), so the independently assembled rowwise family contains \[A=\begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\end{pmatrix}.\] Nevertheless, for every differentiability sequence \(t_k\to0\), \[JF(t_k)=\begin{pmatrix}\operatorname{sign}(t_k)\\\operatorname{sign}(t_k)\end{pmatrix}.\] Any convergent Jacobian sequence therefore has equal rows, and \(A\notin\partial_BF(0)\). This exhibits failure of cross-row compatibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two identical absolute-value components, each sign is individually possible, but opposite row signs cannot occur in one limiting Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\end{pmatrix}\in\mathcal R_F(0)\setminus\partial_BF(0)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Bouligand Directional Derivative
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional B-differentiability via a positively homogeneous first-order model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mapping \(F:U\subset\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is Bouligand differentiable at \(x\in U\) if it is directionally differentiable there, its directional derivative \(F'(x;\cdot)\) is continuous and positively homogeneous, and \[F(x+h)-F(x)-F'(x;h)=o(\|h\|)\qquad(h\to0).\] Here \[F'(x;d):=\lim_{t\downarrow0}\frac{F(x+td)-F(x)}{t}.\] The map \(d\mapsto F'(x;d)\) is the Bouligand derivative of \(F\) at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Bouligand derivative is a continuous positively homogeneous directional model whose residual is little-o of the step norm.
assumptions_latex: The one-sided directional limit exists for every \(d\in\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: one-sided directional derivative at x in direction d
a residual whose norm divided by the step norm tends to zero

children.title: B-Jacobian Matrix Family
children.top_down_role: Matrix-valued local models associated with limiting classical Jacobians.

knowledge_statements.title: B-Jacobian Matrix Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limiting classical Jacobians at nearby differentiability points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:U\subset\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be locally Lipschitz, and let \(D_F\subset U\) be its differentiability set. The B-Jacobian, or Bouligand generalized Jacobian, of \(F\) at \(x\in U\) is \[\partial_BF(x):=\left\{A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}:\text{ there exist }x_k\in D_F,\ x_k\to x,\ JF(x_k)\to A\right\}.\] In finite dimensions local Lipschitz continuity and Rademacher differentiability make this a nonempty compact matrix family. Its convex hull is the Clarke generalized Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The B-Jacobian consists of every limit of ordinary Jacobians evaluated at differentiability points converging to the reference point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial_BF(x)=\operatorname*{Limsup}_{z\to x,\ z\in D_F}\{JF(z)\}\) and \(\partial_CF(x)=\operatorname{co}\partial_BF(x)\).

notation.meaning: set of classical differentiability points of F

children.title: Direction-to-Matrix Correspondence

knowledge_statements.title: Direction-to-Matrix Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Piecewise-smooth realization of each directional derivative by a B-Jacobian matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(F:U\subset\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is locally Lipschitz and piecewise continuously differentiable near \(x\), with finitely many smooth selection functions. Then for every direction \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) there exists a matrix \(A_d\in\partial_BF(x)\) such that \[F'(x;d)=A_dd.\] The realizing matrix may depend on \(d\); the assertion does not require one matrix to represent the directional derivative in every direction. If several selection regions meet the ray from \(x\) in direction \(d\), the realizing matrix need not be unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite piecewise-smooth mapping, every directional derivative equals a B-Jacobian matrix applied to that direction, though the matrix may vary with direction.
assumptions_latex: Near \(x\), \(F\) has finitely many continuously differentiable selections.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall d\in\mathbb R^n\;\exists A_d\in\partial_BF(x):F'(x;d)=A_dd\).

notation.meaning: a B-Jacobian matrix selected for direction d
directional derivative at x along d

children.title: Directional Selection Gaps
children.top_down_role: Cases where directional models cannot be represented by a single coherent matrix selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Directional Selection Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directionwise representability does not imply one globally valid matrix selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\), \(F(t)=|t|\), one has \[\partial_BF(0)=\{-1,1\},\qquad F'(0;d)=|d|.\] For every fixed \(d\), a direction-dependent choice \(A_d=1\) when \(d\ge0\) and \(A_d=-1\) when \(d<0\) satisfies \(F'(0;d)=A_dd\). However, no single \(A\in\partial_BF(0)\) satisfies this identity for every \(d\). Thus exchanging the quantifiers in direction-to-matrix correspondence is invalid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absolute value admits a suitable B-Jacobian sign for each direction, but neither sign represents its derivative in all directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall d\;\exists A_d\in\partial_BF(0):F'(0;d)=A_dd\), but \(\nexists A\in\partial_BF(0)\;\forall d:F'(0;d)=Ad\).

children.title: Newton-Derivative Families

knowledge_statements.title: Newton-Derivative Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Point-dependent linear models evaluated at the perturbed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,Y\) be finite-dimensional normed spaces and \(F:U\subset X\to Y\). A locally bounded mapping \(G:U\to\mathcal L(X,Y)\) is a Newton derivative of \(F\) at \(x\in U\) if \[\|F(x+h)-F(x)-G(x+h)h\|=o(\|h\|)\qquad(h\to0).\] A Newton-derivative family \(\mathcal G\) assigns admissible operators \(\mathcal G(z)\subset\mathcal L(X,Y)\) so that every permitted local selection \(G(z)\in\mathcal G(z)\) under consideration satisfies this approximation condition. The derivative is evaluated at \(x+h\), not necessarily at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Newton derivative uses a point-dependent linear operator at the perturbed point and leaves only a little-o residual.

notation.meaning: space of linear operators from X to Y

knowledge_statements.title: Slant-Derivative Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locally bounded slanting functions furnishing Newton-type residual models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,Y\) be finite-dimensional normed spaces and \(F:U\subset X\to Y\). A mapping \(G:U\to\mathcal L(X,Y)\) is a slanting function for \(F\) at \(x\in U\) if \(G\) is locally bounded near \(x\) and \[\lim_{h\to0,\ h\ne0}\frac{\|F(x+h)-F(x)-G(x+h)h\|}{\|h\|}=0.\] The associated slant-derivative family consists of all operator selections satisfying this condition. Under this convention every slanting function is a Newton derivative at \(x\); terminology may differ when local boundedness is imposed separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A slant derivative is a locally bounded operator-valued model at the perturbed point whose normalized linearization error vanishes.

knowledge_statements.title: Semismooth Derivative Selections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized-Jacobian selections yield Newton approximations for semismooth maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:U\subset\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be locally Lipschitz and directionally differentiable near \(x\). If \(F\) is semismooth at \(x\), then for every sequence \(h_k\to0\) and every choice \(V_k\in\partial_CF(x+h_k)\), \[F(x+h_k)-F(x)-V_kh_k=o(\|h_k\|).\] Consequently, any locally bounded selection \(G(z)\in\partial_CF(z)\) is a Newton derivative at \(x\). If the residual is \(O(\|h\|^{1+\alpha})\) for \(\alpha\in(0,1]\), the corresponding selection has Newton approximation order \(1+\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a semismooth point, every nearby Clarke-Jacobian selection gives a valid Newton model; stronger residual decay gives higher approximation order.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is locally Lipschitz and directionally differentiable near \(x\).

notation.meaning: Clarke generalized Jacobian of F at z

knowledge_statements.title: Graphical-Derivative Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal first-order model obtained from the tangent cone to a multifunction graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S:X\rightrightarrows Y\) be a multifunction between finite-dimensional normed spaces, and let \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}S\). Its graphical derivative at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) is the positively homogeneous multifunction \[DS(\bar x\mid\bar y)(u):=\left\{v\in Y:(u,v)\in T_{\operatorname{gph}S}(\bar x,\bar y)\right\}.\] Equivalently, \(v\in DS(\bar x\mid\bar y)(u)\) when there exist \(t_k\downarrow0\) and \((u_k,v_k)\to(u,v)\) such that \(\bar y+t_kv_k\in S(\bar x+t_ku_k)\) for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The graphical derivative maps an input direction to output directions jointly tangent to the graph of the multifunction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{gph}DS(\bar x\mid\bar y)=T_{\operatorname{gph}S}(\bar x,\bar y)\).

In this regime every contingent graph direction can be realized along every sufficiently small scale, rather than only along a favorable subsequence.

children.title: Tangent-Model Fidelity
children.top_down_role: Faithfulness of graphical first-order models to nearby generalized-equation behavior.

assumptions_latex: The multifunction \(F:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m\) has locally closed graph at \((\bar x,\bar y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The following are equivalent: \(F\) is proto-differentiable at \((\bar x,\bar y)\); and \(\operatorname{gph}F\) is geometrically derivable at \((\bar x,\bar y)\). Under either condition, \[\lim_{t\downarrow0}\frac{\operatorname{gph}F-(\bar x,\bar y)}{t}=T_{\operatorname{gph}F}(\bar x,\bar y)=\operatorname{gph}DF(\bar x,\bar y)\] in the Painlevé--Kuratowski sense. Thus the graphical derivative is not merely an outer tangent approximation: it is the actual two-sided graphical limit of all positive-scale local graph models.

notation.meaning: Painlevé--Kuratowski set limit as positive scale vanishes.
Graphical derivative at the reference graph point.

children.title: Graphical-Regime Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Loss of stable tangent representation under irregular graph geometry.

assumptions_latex: Let \(C:=\{0\}\cup\bigcup_{k\ge0}[2^{-2k-1},2^{-2k}]\subset\mathbb R\) and define \(F:\mathbb R\rightrightarrows\mathbb R\) by \(\operatorname{gph}F=C\times\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At \((0,0)\), the outer tangent cone is \[T_{\operatorname{gph}F}(0,0)=\mathbb R_+\times\{0\},\] while the inner tangent cone is \(T^{\mathrm i}_{\operatorname{gph}F}(0,0)=\{(0,0)\}\). Indeed, favorable scales place any positive horizontal direction in a retained interval, whereas scales centered in the geometric gaps keep a nonvanishing relative distance from the graph. Hence the scaled graphs have distinct outer and inner limits; the graph is not geometrically derivable and \(F\) is not proto-differentiable at \((0,0)\).

notation.meaning: A closed set with alternating retained intervals and geometric gaps.

children.title: Subspace-Containing Derivatives
children.top_down_role: Subspace representations supporting implementable generalized-equation Newton models.

assumptions_latex: The multifunction \(F:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^n\) has locally closed graph, and \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
Let \(\mathcal O_F\) contain graph points \((x,y)\) near \((\bar x,\bar y)\) at which \(T_{\operatorname{gph}F}(x,y)\) is an \(n\)-dimensional linear subspace. The subspace-containing derivative is the family \[\mathscr S F(\bar x,\bar y):=\left\{L:\exists (x_k,y_k)\in\mathcal O_F,
 (x_k,y_k)\to(\bar x,\bar y),
 T_{\operatorname{gph}F}(x_k,y_k)\to L\right\},\] where convergence is in the Grassmannian. Each \(L\) is a limiting linear graph model; unlike a single graphical derivative, the family retains smooth-stratum subspaces approaching the reference point.

notation.meaning: Graph points having an n-dimensional tangent subspace.
An n-dimensional subspace of the product space.

review_flags: The intended SCD variant and its exact convention require a dedicated source.

children.title: Sum Calculus
children.top_down_role: Generalized derivative assembly for additive residual structures.

assumptions_latex: The maps \(F,G:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are Newton differentiable at \(\bar x\), with Newton derivatives \(A_F\) and \(A_G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sum \(H:=F+G\) is Newton differentiable at \(\bar x\), and a Newton derivative is \[A_H(z):=A_F(z)+A_G(z).\] Specifically, as \(h\to0\), \[H(\bar x+h)-H(\bar x)-A_H(\bar x+h)h=o(\lVert h\rVert).\] The same rule extends to a finite linear combination \(\sum_i\alpha_iF_i\) by taking \(A(z)=\sum_i\alpha_iA_{F_i}(z)\), provided every summand satisfies the Newton remainder relation at the common reference point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Newton-derivative sum rule.

knowledge_statements.title: Product Calculus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar pointwise-product rule for locally Lipschitz Newton-differentiable functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The pointwise product \(p:=fg\) is Newton differentiable at \(\bar x\). A Newton derivative is \[a_p(z):=g(z)a_f(z)+f(z)a_g(z).\] Consequently, as \(h\to0\), \[p(\bar x+h)-p(\bar x)-a_p(\bar x+h)h=o(\lVert h\rVert).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For locally Lipschitz Newton-differentiable scalar functions, the product is Newton differentiable and its Newton derivative obeys the Leibniz formula evaluated at the perturbed point.
assumptions_latex: The scalar functions \(f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\) and Newton differentiable at \(\bar x\), with Newton derivatives \(a_f(z),a_g(z)\in\mathbb R^{1\times n}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pointwise product \(p:=fg\) is Newton differentiable at \(\bar x\). A Newton derivative is \[a_p(z):=g(z)a_f(z)+f(z)a_g(z).\] Consequently, as \(h\to0\), \[p(\bar x+h)-p(\bar x)-a_p(\bar x+h)h=o(\lVert h\rVert).\]

children.title: Block Calculus
children.top_down_role: Generalized derivative assembly for partitioned residual systems.

assumptions_latex: For \(i=1,\ldots,q\), the map \(F_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_i}\) is Newton differentiable at \(\bar x\) with Newton derivative \(A_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Define the block mapping \(F(x):=(F_1(x),\ldots,F_q(x))\in\mathbb R^{m_1+\cdots+m_q}\). Then \(F\) is Newton differentiable at \(\bar x\), with block-row Newton derivative \[A_F(z):=\begin{pmatrix}A_1(z)\\ \vdots\\ A_q(z)\end{pmatrix}.\] In the Euclidean product norm, the stacked remainder satisfies \[F(\bar x+h)-F(\bar x)-A_F(\bar x+h)h=o(\lVert h\rVert).\] Thus finitely many component models sharing the same input perturbation form a valid joint block model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite block-row assembly for Newton-differentiable mappings.

children.title: Coupled-Block Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Consistency requirements for derivative choices shared across interacting blocks.

assumptions_latex: The locally Lipschitz mapping \(F=(F_1,ldots,F_q):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_1+\cdots+m_q}\) is differentiable on a dense set near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A tuple \((A_1,\ldots,A_q)\), with \(A_i\in\partial_BF_i(\bar x)\), is coupled-block compatible when there exists one sequence \(x_k\to\bar x\) such that every block is differentiable at \(x_k\) and \[JF_i(x_k)\to A_i\qquad(i=1,\ldots,q).\] Exactly for such tuples, the stacked matrix belongs to the joint Bouligand generalized Jacobian: \[\begin{pmatrix}A_1\\ \vdots\\ A_q\end{pmatrix}\in\partial_BF(\bar x).\] Independent marginal selections need not be compatible because their realizing differentiability sequences may differ.
review_flags: A source explicitly treating simultaneous block realizability is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous-sequence compatibility for Bouligand block selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A tuple \((A_1,\ldots,A_q)\), with \(A_i\in\partial_BF_i(\bar x)\), is coupled-block compatible when there exists one sequence \(x_k\to\bar x\) such that every block is differentiable at \(x_k\) and \[JF_i(x_k)\to A_i\qquad(i=1,\ldots,q).\] Exactly for such tuples, the stacked matrix belongs to the joint Bouligand generalized Jacobian: \[\begin{pmatrix}A_1\\ \vdots\\ A_q\end{pmatrix}\in\partial_BF(\bar x).\] Independent marginal selections need not be compatible because their realizing differentiability sequences may differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block derivative selections are compatible precisely when one common differentiability sequence realizes all blocks simultaneously; independent marginal selections may fail this requirement.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupled-Block Compatibility

knowledge_statements.title: Composition Calculus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Newton-derivative composition rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(H:=G\circ F\), define \[A_H(z):=A_G(F(z))A_F(z).\] Then \(H\) is Newton differentiable at \(\bar x\), and \[H(\bar x+h)-H(\bar x)-A_H(\bar x+h)h=o(\lVert h\rVert).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under local Lipschitz and boundedness conditions, composing Newton-differentiable maps yields a Newton derivative equal to the product of the outer and inner models.
assumptions_latex: The map \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is Newton differentiable at \(\bar x\), and \(G:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^p\) is Newton differentiable at \(F(\bar x)\).
The map \(F\) is locally Lipschitz at \(\bar x\), and the selected Newton derivatives of \(G\) are locally bounded near \(F(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(H:=G\circ F\), define \[A_H(z):=A_G(F(z))A_F(z).\] Then \(H\) is Newton differentiable at \(\bar x\), and \[H(\bar x+h)-H(\bar x)-A_H(\bar x+h)h=o(\lVert h\rVert).\]

children.title: Generalized Chain Rules
children.top_down_role: Structural relations connecting derivative families across inner and outer maps.

assumptions_latex: The maps \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) and \(G:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^p\) are locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\) and \(F(\bar x)\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For the Clarke generalized Jacobian, the composite \(H:=G\circ F\) satisfies the chain-rule inclusion \[\partial_C H(\bar x)\subseteq\operatorname{co}\{BA:A\in\partial_CF(\bar x),\ B\in\partial_CG(F(\bar x))\}.\] Here matrix multiplication follows the order of composition. The right-hand side generally overestimates the joint limits because independently selected \(A\) and \(B\) need not arise along a common differentiability sequence. Additional regularity or compatible active structure is therefore needed before replacing the inclusion by equality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clarke generalized-Jacobian chain-rule inclusion in finite dimensions.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is locally Lipschitz and piecewise \(C^1\) near \(\bar x\), with local selections \(F_i\).
\(G:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}^p\) is locally Lipschitz and piecewise \(C^1\) near \(F(\bar x)\), with local selections \(G_j\).
Every locally active pair \((i,j)\) is jointly attainable by a sequence approaching \(\bar x\) through differentiability points of \(G\circ F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial_B(G\circ F)(\bar x)=\left\{\nabla G_j(F(\bar x))\nabla F_i(\bar x):(i,j)\in\mathcal A_{G\circ F}(\bar x)\right\}.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_i\) and \(G_j\) be the smooth local pieces representing \(F\) and \(G\). A pair \((i,j)\) is jointly attainable at \(\bar x\) when there are differentiability points \(x_k\to\bar x\) for which \(F=F_i\) near \(x_k\), \(G=G_j\) near \(F(x_k)\), and the associated Jacobians converge. Under the stated joint-attainability condition, the limiting Jacobians of the composition are exactly the compatible products: \[\partial_B(G\circ F)(\bar x)=\left\{\nabla G_j(F(\bar x))\nabla F_i(\bar x):(i,j)\in\mathcal A_{G\circ F}(\bar x)\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For piecewise-smooth maps, the limiting Jacobians of a composition are exactly products from jointly attainable inner and outer active pieces.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be a locally Lipschitz inverse branch satisfying \(G(F(x))=x\) near \(\bar x\). Nonsingularity of every \(A\in\partial_CF(\bar x)\) yields the inverse-Jacobian estimate \[\partial_CG(\bar y)\subseteq\operatorname{co}\left\{A^{-1}:A\in\partial_CF(\bar x)\right\}.\] Thus generalized derivatives of the inverse are controlled by inverses of generalized derivatives of the original mapping. The convex hull and inclusion cannot generally be removed without stronger structural or coherent-selection assumptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Branch Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Lipschitz bound for an implicit branch under a Clarke block-derivative inclusion and uniform state-block conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s\) be a locally Lipschitz implicit solution branch. If its Clarke generalized Jacobian is contained in the convex hull of the blockwise matrices \(-B^{-1}A\), with \(\|B^{-1}\|\leq\kappa\) and \(\|A\|\leq L_u\) for every contributing block pair, then \[\operatorname{lip}s(\bar u)\leq\kappa L_u.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every generalized derivative of a locally Lipschitz implicit branch is generated by parameter and state blocks whose norms are uniformly bounded by L_u and κ, respectively, then the branch's local Lipschitz modulus is at most κL_u.
assumptions_latex: \(H:\mathbb{R}^p\times\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is locally Lipschitz near \((\bar u,\bar x)\), and \(H(\bar u,\bar x)=0\).
\(s\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar u\), satisfies \(s(\bar u)=\bar x\), and obeys \(H(u,s(u))=0\) locally.
For every \([A\ B]\in\partial_CH(\bar u,\bar x)\), the matrix \(B\) is invertible, \(\|B^{-1}\|\leq\kappa\), and \(\|A\|\leq L_u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{lip}s(\bar u)\leq\kappa L_u.\]

notation.meaning: Parameter and state blocks of a generalized Jacobian of the equation map.
Exact local Lipschitz modulus of the branch at the reference parameter.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A singular attainable state block marks the boundary of the standard implicit-branch calculus. If \([A\ B]\in\partial_BH(\bar u,\bar x)\) and \(B\) is singular, then the formula \(-B^{-1}A\) is undefined for that selection, and inverse norms of nearby nonsingular state blocks need not be bounded. Consequently neither local single-valuedness nor a finite Lipschitz sensitivity modulus follows from the usual generalized-Jacobian argument; branch merging, branching, or unbounded sensitivity may occur.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An attainable singular state block invalidates the standard implicit derivative formula and may coincide with branching, loss of uniqueness, or unbounded sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular Branch Boundaries

children.title: Projection Derivative Families
children.top_down_role: Generalized derivative objects associated with projection mappings.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty closed convex polyhedral set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[P_C'(x;h)=P_{K}(h),\qquad K=T_C(p)\cap r^\perp.\]

notation.meaning: Euclidean projector onto a closed convex set.
Critical cone determined by the projection residual.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional derivative of Euclidean projection onto a convex polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p=P_C(x)\), define the projection residual \(r=x-p\) and critical cone \(K=T_C(p)\cap r^\perp\). The Euclidean projector onto a convex polyhedral set is directionally differentiable at every \(x\), and its directional derivative is the projector onto the critical cone: \[P_C'(x;h)=P_K(h)\qquad\text{for every }h\in\mathbb{R}^n.\] As \(h\) moves between polyhedral sectors, the corresponding linear projector selections form a piecewise-linear derivative family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex polyhedron, the directional derivative of its projector is projection onto the critical cone determined by the base projection and residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection Derivative Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The polyhedral critical-cone projection formula is standard and fits the representation leaf, but no source or inspectable theorem locator is supplied.

children.title: Proximal Derivative Families
children.top_down_role: Generalized derivative objects associated with proximal mappings.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, convex, and twice epi-differentiable at \(p\) for \(v\in\partial f(p)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[D\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)(h)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{w}\left\{\frac12\|w-h\|^2+\frac{\lambda}{2}d_e^2f(p\mid v)(w)\right\}.\]

notation.meaning: Second epi-derivative of \(f\) at \(p\) relative to \(v\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex proximal derivative represented by a second epi-derivative subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under twice epi-differentiability, the proximal mapping is directionally differentiable at \(x\). For each direction \(h\), its derivative is the unique minimizer \[D\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)(h)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{w\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{\frac12\|w-h\|^2+\frac{\lambda}{2}d_e^2f(p\mid v)(w)\right\}.\] Thus the local derivative family is itself a family of proximal-type solution operators generated by the second-order variational model at \((p,v)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a convex function is twice epi-differentiable, each directional derivative of its proximal map solves a strongly convex second-order model problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Derivative Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proximal derivative representation depends on the convention used for the second epi-derivative and on the exact theorem linking twice epi-differentiability to directional differentiability. No source is supplied to settle those points.

children.title: Resolvent Derivative Families
children.top_down_role: Generalized derivative objects associated with resolvent mappings.

assumptions_latex: \(A:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^n\) is maximal monotone and proto-differentiable at \((p,v)\in\operatorname{gph}A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[w=J_{\lambda A}'(x;h)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad h-w\in\lambda DA(p\mid v)(w).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resolvent directional derivative through the graphical derivative of a maximal monotone operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The resolvent identity \(x-p\in\lambda A(p)\) linearizes through the graphical derivative of \(A\). For every direction \(h\), a derivative value \(w\) is characterized by \[w=J_{\lambda A}'(x;h)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad h-w\in\lambda DA(p\mid v)(w).\] Equivalently, whenever the linearized resolvent is single-valued, \(J_{\lambda A}'(x;\cdot)=(I+\lambda DA(p\mid v))^{-1}\). Different graphical-derivative selections therefore generate the local resolvent derivative family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A resolvent derivative is obtained by solving the resolvent inclusion for the graphical derivative of the underlying maximal monotone operator.
knowledge_statements.title: Resolvent Derivative Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The graphical-derivative resolvent inclusion is plausible and appropriately classified as a representation, but an authoritative source is required to confirm that the stated proto-differentiability assumptions suffice for the asserted single-valued directional derivative.

children.title: Curvature-Sensitive Primitive Calculus
children.top_down_role: Derivative behavior influenced by nonpolyhedral or curved underlying geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, convex, twice epi-differentiable at \(p\) for \(v\in\partial f(p)\).
\(Q\) is self-adjoint positive semidefinite and \(K\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[D\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)(h)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{w\in K}\left\{\frac12\|w-h\|^2+\frac{\lambda}{2}\langle w,Qw\rangle\right\}.\]

notation.meaning: Curvature operator in the second epi-derivative.
Critical cone encoded by the second epi-derivative.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primitive proximal calculus when the second-order model separates into curvature and a critical cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When the second epi-derivative decomposes as \(d_e^2f(p\mid v)(w)=\langle w,Qw\rangle+\delta_K(w)\), the proximal directional derivative is the unique curvature-corrected critical-cone projection \[D\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)(h)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{w\in K}\left\{\frac12\|w-h\|^2+\frac{\lambda}{2}\langle w,Qw\rangle\right\}.\] The cone \(K\) records first-order activity, whereas \(Q\) records second-order curvature; omitting \(Q\) generally changes the derivative whenever the active geometry is curved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structured second epi-derivative turns the proximal derivative into projection onto a critical cone corrected by a quadratic curvature term.
knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Sensitive Primitive Calculus

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The curvature-corrected critical-cone formula follows only after fixing the normalization of the second epi-derivative and verifying the proximal derivative theorem. No supporting source or locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: B-Derivative Selection from Essentially Active Pieces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: B-derivatives and, when present, classical derivatives of a PC^1 map are selected from essentially active smooth pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let V\subset\mathbb{R}^n be open. Suppose the PC^1 map f:V\to\mathbb{R}^m is a continuous selection of C^1 maps \{f^1,\ldots,f^N\} on a neighborhood W of x\in V. Then f is B-differentiable at x and, for every y\in\mathbb{R}^n, f'(x;y)\in\{(f^i)'(x)y:i\in I^e(x)\}. If f is classically differentiable at x, then f'(x)\in\{(f^i)'(x):i\in I^e(x)\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A piecewise C^1 map is B-differentiable at the reference point, and each directional derivative is generated by an essentially active smooth piece. If the map is classically differentiable there, its Jacobian equals that of an essentially active piece.

children.top_down_role: Selection of local matrices from convexified generalized Jacobian families.

knowledge_statements.title: Convexified-Jacobian Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clarke selection for a locally Lipschitz finite-dimensional mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\), and let \(D_F\) denote its differentiability set. Define \(\partial_BF(\bar x)=\{\lim_k JF(x_k):x_k\in D_F,\ x_k\to\bar x\}\). A convexified-Jacobian selection at \(\bar x\) is any matrix \(A\) satisfying \[A\in\partial_CF(\bar x):=\operatorname{co}\partial_BF(\bar x).\] Thus \(A\) may be a convex combination of limiting Jacobians without itself being attainable as a limiting classical Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convexified selection is any matrix in the Clarke generalized Jacobian, the convex hull of all limiting classical Jacobians.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\text{ is a convexified-Jacobian selection}\iff A\in\partial_CF(\bar x)=\operatorname{co}\partial_BF(\bar x).\)

knowledge_statements.title: Extreme-Point Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extreme selections from a compact limiting-Jacobian set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\). Since \(\partial_BF(\bar x)\) is compact in finite dimensions and \(\partial_CF(\bar x)=\operatorname{co}\partial_BF(\bar x)\), every extreme point of the Clarke generalized Jacobian is a limiting Jacobian: \[\operatorname{ext}\partial_CF(\bar x)\subseteq\partial_BF(\bar x).\] Consequently, selecting an extreme point of \(\partial_CF(\bar x)\) avoids a matrix created solely by nontrivial convex averaging, although different extreme selections may still represent different limiting smooth pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every extreme point of the Clarke generalized Jacobian is a limiting Jacobian, so extreme selection avoids purely averaged matrices.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\in\operatorname{ext}\partial_CF(\bar x)\Longrightarrow A\in\partial_BF(\bar x).\)

knowledge_statements.title: Convexification-Induced Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A convexified scalar Jacobian that is not a valid first-order selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(F:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\), \(F(x)=|x|\), at \(\bar x=0\). Its limiting and Clarke Jacobians are \[\partial_BF(0)=\{-1,1\},\qquad \partial_CF(0)=[-1,1].\] Convexification admits \(A=0\), but this matrix does not model any nonzero increment to first order: \[F(h)-F(0)-Ah=|h|,\qquad \frac{|F(h)-F(0)-Ah|}{|h|}=1\quad(h\ne0).\] Hence membership in the convexified Jacobian alone does not make a fixed selection a Newton derivative or a coherent active-piece linearization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the absolute-value map, zero belongs to the Clarke Jacobian but gives a first-order error equal to the entire increment size.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial_CF(0)\setminus\partial_BF(0)\) and \(F(h)-F(0)-0h\ne o(|h|).\)

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Selection Coherence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequence-coupled chain-rule selection for a composite mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=H\circ G\), where \(G:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\) and \(H:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R^m\) are locally Lipschitz. A pair \((A,B)\) is a coherent composite selection at \(\bar x\) if there exists one sequence \(x_k\to\bar x\) such that both mappings are differentiable at the required points and \[JG(x_k)\to A,\qquad JH(G(x_k))\to B.\] The induced composite matrix is \(V=BA\). Because \(J(H\circ G)(x_k)=JH(G(x_k))JG(x_k)\), this coupling guarantees \(V\in\partial_BF(\bar x)\). Independently chosen factors need not have this property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composite selections are coherent when both derivative factors arise along the same primal sequence; their product is then a limiting composite Jacobian.
assumptions_latex: \(F=H\circ G\), with \(G\) and \(H\) locally Lipschitz near the relevant points.
\(G(x_k)\) is a differentiability point of \(H\), and \(x_k\) is a differentiability point of \(G\) and \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(JG(x_k)\to A\ \land\ JH(G(x_k))\to B\Longrightarrow BA\in\partial_BF(\bar x).\)

knowledge_statements.title: Block Selection Coherence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common-sequence condition for a vertically blocked mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=(F_1,\ldots,F_q):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_1+\cdots+m_q}\) be locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\). A block matrix \(A=(A_1^\top,\ldots,A_q^\top)^\top\) is a coherent block selection if one sequence \(x_k\to\bar x\) consists of common differentiability points and satisfies \[JF_i(x_k)\to A_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,q).\] Then \(JF(x_k)\to A\), so \(A\in\partial_BF(\bar x)\). Merely requiring each \(A_i\in\partial_BF_i(\bar x)\) is insufficient because the witnessing sequences may be incompatible across blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block Jacobian is coherent when every block limit is generated by the same sequence of differentiability points.
assumptions_latex: \(x_k\to\bar x\) consists of common differentiability points of all blocks and of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(JF_i(x_k)\to A_i\ (i=1,\ldots,q)\Longrightarrow (A_1^\top,\ldots,A_q^\top)^\top\in\partial_BF(\bar x).\)

knowledge_statements.title: Shared Active-Index Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-piece selections constrained by a common piece index.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=(F_1,\ldots,F_q):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_1+\cdots+m_q}\) have a common finite piece representation: for each relevant \(x\), \[F(x)=F^{\alpha}(x)=\bigl(F_1^{\alpha}(x),\ldots,F_q^{\alpha}(x)\bigr)\quad\text{whenever }\alpha\in I(x),\] where every \(F_i^{\alpha}\) is differentiable near \(\bar x\). A block selection is coupled through a shared active index at \(\bar x\) if there exists \(\alpha\in I(\bar x)\) such that \[A_i=JF_i^{\alpha}(\bar x)\quad(i=1,\ldots,q).\] For \(A=(A_1^\top,\ldots,A_q^\top)^\top\), this condition gives \(A=JF^{\alpha}(\bar x)\). Selections using separate indices are coherent only when one locally realizable piece induces all selected block derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When all blocks share a piecewise-smooth regime, shared active-index coupling means using one simultaneously active piece for every block; the assembled matrix is the Jacobian of that piece.
assumptions_latex: \(F=(F_1,\ldots,F_q):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_1+\cdots+m_q}\) has a common finite piece representation.
\(I(\bar x)\) is a finite set of active indices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\alpha\in I(\bar x)\ \forall i\in\{1,\ldots,q\}: A_i=JF_i^{\alpha}(\bar x)\Longrightarrow A=(A_1^\top,\ldots,A_q^\top)^\top=JF^{\alpha}(\bar x).\)

children.title: Cross-Block Selection Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Incompatible local models caused by independently selected block derivatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Block Selection Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent block selection can create a nonexistent full Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(F:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^2\) by \(F(x)=(\max\{x,0\},\min\{x,0\})\). At \(0\), \[\partial_BF(0)=\left\{\binom{1}{0},\binom{0}{1}\right\},\qquad \partial_CF(0)=\left\{\binom{t}{1-t}:0\le t\le1\right\}.\] Independent componentwise selection can choose derivative \(1\) for both blocks, producing \(A=(1,1)^\top\). Yet \(A\notin\partial_CF(0)\), because the first derivative occurs only when approaching from the right and the second only when approaching from the left. Thus the assembled selection has no common generating sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Opposite one-sided regimes let each block select derivative one, although the assembled vector is not even a Clarke Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(1\in\partial_BF_1(0)\ \land\ 1\in\partial_BF_2(0)\), but \(\binom{1}{1}\notin\partial_CF(0).\)

knowledge_statements.title: Selection-Mismatch Pathologies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between individually admissible and jointly realizable derivative selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a locally Lipschitz blocked or composite mapping, individual membership of selected factors or rows in their respective limiting-Jacobian sets does not ensure that the assembled matrix belongs to the limiting or Clarke Jacobian of the full mapping. Validity requires joint realizability, such as a common differentiability sequence or a shared active piece. In particular, for \(F(x)=(\max\{x,0\},\min\{x,0\})\), independent row selection yields \(A=(1,1)^\top\), while \[A\notin\partial_CF(0)=\left\{(t,1-t)^\top:0\le t\le1\right\}.\] Such a mismatch invalidates generalized-Jacobian membership and any Newton model justified solely by that membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Individually valid rows or factors may be jointly impossible; without a common regime, their assembly can fall outside the full generalized Jacobian.
assumptions_latex: The mapping is locally Lipschitz and is represented by multiple blocks or composite factors.
Selections are made independently, without a common generating sequence or active piece.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_i\in\partial_BF_i(\bar x)\ \forall i\centernot\Longrightarrow A\in\partial_CF(\bar x).\)

children.title: BD-Regular Regime

knowledge_statements.title: BD-Regular Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonsingularity over limiting Jacobians at a root.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\). The mapping is BD-regular at \(\bar x\) if every limiting Jacobian is nonsingular: \[\det V\ne0\qquad\text{for every }V\in\partial_BF(\bar x).\] Because \(\partial_BF(\bar x)\) is compact, this pointwise condition is equivalent to a uniform inverse bound on that set: \[\sup_{V\in\partial_BF(\bar x)}\|V^{-1}\|<\infty,\] with the supremum understood only over the nonempty limiting-Jacobian set. BD-regularity does not require every convex combination in \(\partial_CF(\bar x)\) to be nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: BD-regularity requires every limiting Jacobian at the point to be invertible, equivalently with uniformly bounded inverses on that compact set.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\text{ is BD-regular at }\bar x\iff\forall V\in\partial_BF(\bar x),\ \det V\ne0.\)

notation.meaning: operator norm of the inverse matrix

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Uniform Invertibility under Strong BD-Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighborhood persistence of nonsingularity and uniform boundedness of inverses for B-subdifferential selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(F\) is strongly BD-regular at \(z\), then there exist a neighborhood \(\mathcal U\) of \(z\) and a constant \(c\ge 0\) such that, for every \(v\in\mathcal U\) and every \(V\in\partial_BF(v)\), \(V\) is nonsingular and \(\lVert V^{-1}\rVert\le c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong BD-regularity at z implies that every nearby B-subdifferential matrix is nonsingular and that all their inverses are uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\mathcal U\ni z\;\exists c\ge0\;\forall v\in\mathcal U\;\forall V\in\partial_BF(v):\quad V\text{ is nonsingular and }\lVert V^{-1}\rVert\le c.

knowledge_statements.title: CD-Regular Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonsingularity over the Clarke generalized Jacobian at a root.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\). The mapping is CD-regular at \(\bar x\) if \[\det V\ne0\qquad\text{for every }V\in\partial_CF(\bar x).\] Compactness of \(\partial_CF(\bar x)\) then gives \(\sup_{V\in\partial_CF(\bar x)}\|V^{-1}\|<\infty\). Since \(\partial_BF(\bar x)\subseteq\partial_CF(\bar x)\), CD-regularity implies BD-regularity. The converse can fail because a convex combination of nonsingular limiting Jacobians may be singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CD-regularity requires every Clarke generalized Jacobian to be invertible; it implies BD-regularity but is generally stronger.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\text{ is CD-regular at }\bar x\iff\forall V\in\partial_CF(\bar x),\ \det V\ne0.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Model Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invertibility of every admissible model matrix at one base point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be a nonempty compact-valued local derivative model for \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\). The model is pointwise regular at \(\bar x\) if every matrix admitted exactly at \(\bar x\) is nonsingular: \[\inf_{A\in\mathcal M(\bar x)}\sigma_{\min}(A)>0.\] For compact \(\mathcal M(\bar x)\), this is equivalent to \(\det A\ne0\) for every \(A\in\mathcal M(\bar x)\), or to \(\sup_{A\in\mathcal M(\bar x)}\|A^{-1}\|<\infty\). It imposes no condition on matrices appearing only at nearby points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise model regularity means that all model matrices admitted at the base point are uniformly nonsingular there.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M(\bar x)\subset\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is nonempty and compact.
\(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) has local derivative model \(\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{A\in\mathcal M(\bar x)}\sigma_{\min}(A)>0.\)

notation.meaning: set of admissible local model matrices at x

children.title: Sequential Model Regularity
children.top_down_role: Regularity assessed across nearby sequences of admissible local models.

knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Model Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform nonsingularity along every convergent sequence of model selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be a local derivative model. It is sequentially regular at \(\bar x\) if, for every sequence \(x_k\to\bar x\) and every selection \(A_k\in\mathcal M(x_k)\), \[\liminf_{k\to\infty}\sigma_{\min}(A_k)>0.\] Equivalently, along every such selected sequence the inverse norms are eventually bounded: \(\limsup_k\|A_k^{-1}\|<\infty\). Constant sequences show that sequential regularity implies pointwise model regularity. The converse can fail when nonsingular matrices admitted at \(\bar x\) are approached by nearly singular matrices admitted at neighboring points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential regularity requires every nearby sequence of selected model matrices to remain uniformly away from singularity.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M(x)\subseteq\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is nonempty for all x sufficiently near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall x_k\to\bar x\ \forall A_k\in\mathcal M(x_k),\ \liminf_k\sigma_{\min}(A_k)>0.\)

notation.meaning: set of admissible local model matrices at x

children.title: Uniform Neighborhood Regularity
children.top_down_role: Stable nonsingularity behavior across a full local neighborhood.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Neighborhood Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform nonsingularity of Clarke generalized Jacobians near a reference root.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\). Its generalized-Jacobian model is uniformly regular near \(\bar x\) if there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(\gamma>0\) such that
\[
\|A^{-1}\|\leq \gamma
\quad\text{for every }x\in U\text{ and }A\in\partial_C F(x).
\]
Thus every nearby model matrix is nonsingular with a common inverse bound. Equivalently, \(\inf_{x\in U,\,A\in\partial_C F(x)}\sigma_{\min}(A)>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every Clarke model matrix at every sufficiently nearby point is invertible, and their inverse norms share one finite bound.
assumptions_latex: F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is locally Lipschitz near }\bar x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U\ni\bar x,\ \exists\gamma>0:\ \sup_{x\in U,\,A\in\partial_C F(x)}\|A^{-1}\|\leq\gamma

notation.meaning: Clarke generalized Jacobian of F at x

children.title: Sequence-Induced Singularity

knowledge_statements.title: Sequence-Induced Singularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential witness for loss of uniform generalized-Jacobian regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\). Uniform neighborhood regularity fails precisely when there exist sequences \(x_k\to\bar x\), \(A_k\in\partial_C F(x_k)\), and \(d_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \(\|d_k\|=1\) and \(\|A_kd_k\|\to0\). The matrices need not be singular individually: their smallest singular values may merely converge to zero, producing asymptotically singular local models.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform regularity fails exactly when nearby generalized Jacobians possess unit directions whose images converge to zero.
assumptions_latex: F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is locally Lipschitz near }\bar x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \neg\operatorname{UNR}(F,\bar x)\iff\exists x_k\to\bar x,\ A_k\in\partial_C F(x_k),\ \|d_k\|=1,\ A_kd_k\to0

notation.meaning: uniform neighborhood regularity at the reference point

knowledge_statements.title: Coherent Orientation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Determinant-sign condition for square piecewise-affine local models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuous and piecewise affine on a finite polyhedral subdivision, with \(M(x)=A_i x+b_i\) on each full-dimensional cell \(P_i\). The model is coherently oriented on a neighborhood \(U\) if every cell whose interior meets \(U\) has \(\det A_i\neq0\), and there exists \(s\in\{-1,1\}\) such that \(\operatorname{sign}(\det A_i)=s\) for all such cells. Hence all active affine selections are nonsingular and have the same orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A piecewise-affine model is coherently oriented when all locally active selection matrices are nonsingular and their determinants have one common sign.
assumptions_latex: M:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is continuous and piecewise affine}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists s\in\{-1,1\}:\ \operatorname{sign}(\det A_i)=s\ \text{ for every locally active }A_i

notation.meaning: linear part of the affine selection on the cell

children.title: Metric Regularity
children.top_down_role: Open-mapping and inverse-stability behavior relevant to perturbed equation solving.

knowledge_statements.title: Metric Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local inverse-stability definition for finite-dimensional set-valued mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\) and let \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\). The mapping \(F\) is metrically regular at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar y\) if there exist neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\), \(V\) of \(\bar y\), and \(\kappa\geq0\) such that
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,F^{-1}(y))\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(y,F(x))
\quad (x\in U,\ y\in V).
\]
Distances to the empty set are interpreted as \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric regularity bounds the distance to a perturbed solution set by the residual distance, uniformly for nearby points and right-hand sides.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U,V,\kappa:\ \operatorname{dist}(x,F^{-1}(y))\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(y,F(x))\quad(x\in U,\ y\in V)

notation.meaning: graph of the set-valued mapping F
set of x such that y belongs to F(x)

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Metric Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric regularity strengthened by a single-valued Lipschitz inverse localization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\) and \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\). The mapping \(F\) is strongly metrically regular at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar y\) if there are neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(V\) of \(\bar y\) such that
\[
s(y):=F^{-1}(y)\cap U
\]
is a singleton for every \(y\in V\), and the resulting function \(s:V\to U\) is Lipschitz with \(s(\bar y)=\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong metric regularity means nearby right-hand sides have a unique nearby solution that depends Lipschitz-continuously on the right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U,V:\ y\mapsto F^{-1}(y)\cap U\text{ is single-valued and Lipschitz on }V

children.title: Robinson Strong Regularity
children.top_down_role: Linearized generalized-equation regularity and its Newton interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Robinson Strong Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong regularity of a generalized equation through its partially linearized inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(0\in f(x)+Q(x)\), where \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is continuously differentiable near a solution \(\bar x\) and \(Q:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\). The solution is Robinson strongly regular if neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(V\) of \(0\) exist such that, for every \(y\in V\),
\[
y\in f(\bar x)+Df(\bar x)(x-\bar x)+Q(x),\qquad x\in U,
\]
has exactly one solution \(x=s(y)\), and \(s\) is Lipschitz on \(V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robinson strong regularity requires the partially linearized generalized equation to have a unique nearby solution depending Lipschitz-continuously on perturbations.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\text{ is continuously differentiable near }\bar x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y\mapsto\{x\in U:y\in f(\bar x)+Df(\bar x)(x-\bar x)+Q(x)\}\text{ is single-valued and Lipschitz near }0

notation.meaning: set-valued term of the generalized equation
localized solution of the linearized inclusion

knowledge_statements.title: Metric Subregularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-right-hand-side error bound for a set-valued mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\) and \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\). The mapping \(F\) is metrically subregular at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar y\) if there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(\kappa\geq0\) such that
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,F^{-1}(\bar y))\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,F(x))
\quad\text{for every }x\in U.
\]
Unlike metric regularity, the target value remains fixed at \(\bar y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric subregularity controls distance to the nearby solution set using the residual for one fixed target value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U\ni\bar x,\ \exists\kappa\geq0:\ \operatorname{dist}(x,F^{-1}(\bar y))\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,F(x))\quad(x\in U)

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Metric Subregularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-target residual bound relative to an isolated reference solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\) and \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\). The mapping \(F\) is strongly metrically subregular at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar y\) if there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(\kappa\geq0\) such that
\[
\|x-\bar x\|\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,F(x))
\quad\text{for every }x\in U.
\]
This inequality implies \(F^{-1}(\bar y)\cap U=\{\bar x\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong metric subregularity bounds distance to the reference solution itself and consequently makes that solution locally isolated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U\ni\bar x,\ \exists\kappa\geq0:\ \|x-\bar x\|\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,F(x))\quad(x\in U)

notation.meaning: residual distance from the target to the image

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Set Error Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local residual inequality measuring distance to the full solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\), a graph point \((\bar x,\bar y)\), and \(S:=F^{-1}(\bar y)\), solution-set error control holds locally if there are \(\kappa\geq0\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) such that
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,F(x))
\quad\text{for all }x\in U.
\]
The left side permits multiple nearby solutions; the condition is exactly the local error-bound form of metric subregularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The residual controls distance to the entire solution set, without requiring the reference solution to be isolated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,F(x))\quad\text{locally at }\bar x

notation.meaning: solution set for the fixed target value

children.title: Isolated-Solution Error Control
children.top_down_role: Error-control consequences tied to local isolation of the reference solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Isolated-Solution Error Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local residual inequality measuring distance to one isolated solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\). Isolated-solution error control holds if there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(\kappa\geq0\) such that
\[
\|x-\bar x\|\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,F(x))
\quad\text{for all }x\in U.
\]
Substitution of any \(x\in F^{-1}(\bar y)\cap U\) forces \(x=\bar x\); hence the inequality simultaneously certifies local isolation and gives a quantitative residual estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The residual controls distance to one reference solution and certifies that no other solution lies sufficiently nearby.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|x-\bar x\|\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,F(x))\text{ locally, and }F^{-1}(\bar y)\cap U=\{\bar x\}

children.title: Residual Error Bounds
children.top_down_role: Local distance certificates based on equation residual magnitude.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Error Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable local distance certificate for a single-valued nonsmooth equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), let \(S:=\{x:R(x)=0\}\), and take \(\bar x\in S\). A local residual error-bound certificate consists of \(\kappa\geq0\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) satisfying
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\|R(x)\|
\quad\text{for every }x\in U.
\]
Consequently, evaluating \(\|R(x)\|\) at any \(x\in U\) certifies the upper bound \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\|R(x)\|\) on the distance to the solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual norm, multiplied by a known error-bound constant, certifies an upper bound on distance to the solution set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\in U\implies\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\|R(x)\|

children.title: Piecewise-Polyhedral Error Bounds
children.top_down_role: Error-bound regimes inherited from piecewise-polyhedral residuals and inclusions.

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise-Polyhedral Error Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local error bound for continuous piecewise-affine residual equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be continuous and piecewise affine on a finite polyhedral subdivision, and let \(S:=R^{-1}(0)\). For every \(\bar x\in S\), there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and a constant \(\kappa\geq0\) such that
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\|R(x)\|
\quad\text{for all }x\in U.
\]
Thus piecewise-polyhedral residual geometry yields metric subregularity at each zero, although it does not by itself imply that the zero is isolated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every zero of a finite continuous piecewise-affine residual admits a local solution-set error bound, but need not be isolated.
assumptions_latex: R:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\text{ is continuous and piecewise affine on finitely many polyhedral cells}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U\ni\bar x,\ \exists\kappa\geq0:\ \operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\|R(x)\|\quad(x\in U)

notation.meaning: zero set of the piecewise-affine residual

children.title: Isolated-Root Geometry
children.top_down_role: Local regularity and model behavior around isolated solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Isolated-Root Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong metric subregularity expressed as isolated-root residual geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be continuous near \(\bar x\), with \(F(\bar x)=0\). The root \(\bar x\) has isolated-root error-bound geometry if there exist \(\kappa>0\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) such that
\[
\|x-\bar x\|\leq \kappa\|F(x)\|\qquad(x\in U).
\]
This inequality implies \(F^{-1}(0)\cap U=\{\bar x\}\) and is precisely strong metric subregularity of \(F\) at \((\bar x,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A root has isolated-root error-bound geometry when, locally, its displacement from the root is bounded by a constant times the residual norm; this condition also makes the root locally unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|x-\bar x\|\leq\kappa\|F(x)\|\text{ locally, and }F^{-1}(0)\cap U=\{\bar x\}

children.title: Nonisolated Solution Geometry
children.top_down_role: Rank-deficient, manifold-like, and set-valued local solution structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonisolated Solution Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant-rank local model for manifold-like, nonisolated zero sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\), with \(F(\bar x)=0\), and suppose \(\operatorname{rank}DF(x)=r\) throughout a neighborhood of \(\bar x\). Then, after shrinking the neighborhood, the solution set \(S=F^{-1}(0)\) is a \(C^1\) embedded manifold of dimension \(n-r\),
\[
T_S(\bar x)=\ker DF(\bar x),
\]
and there exist \(\kappa>0\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) such that \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\|F(x)\|\) for every \(x\in U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant-rank equation has a local solution manifold whose tangent space is the derivative kernel, together with a residual error bound to that manifold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ is a }C^1\text{ manifold, }\dim S=n-r,\ T_S(\bar x)=\ker DF(\bar x),\ \operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\|F(x)\|

notation.meaning: Local zero set of the equation.
Tangent space to the solution manifold.

children.title: Regularity Under Equation Reformulation
children.top_down_role: Comparison of regularity for original systems, natural residuals, normal maps, and complementarity equations.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularity Under Equation Reformulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of residual error bounds between locally equivalent equation formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R,Q:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\) satisfy \(R^{-1}(0)\cap U=Q^{-1}(0)\cap U=:S\) on a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\in S\). If constants \(0<c\leq C<\infty\) satisfy
\[
c\|R(x)\|\leq\|Q(x)\|\leq C\|R(x)\|\qquad(x\in U),
\]
then a local error bound for either formulation holds if and only if it holds for the other. Specifically, \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa_R\|R(x)\|\) implies \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq(\kappa_R/c)\|Q(x)\|\), while the reverse implication has modulus \(C\kappa_Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two reformulations with identical local zeros and uniformly equivalent residual norms possess equivalent local error-bound regularity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R\text{ has a local residual error bound }\Longleftrightarrow Q\text{ has one}

children.title: Regularity Under Smooth Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Stability of local solvability under perturbations of smooth equation components.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularity Under Smooth Perturbations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Small-Lipschitz perturbation theorem for strong metric regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^n\) be strongly metrically regular at \((\bar x,\bar y)\), with a single-valued inverse localization having Lipschitz modulus \(\kappa\). Let \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be \(C^1\) near \(\bar x\) and locally Lipschitz with modulus \(\lambda\), where \(\kappa\lambda<1\). Then \(F+g\) is strongly metrically regular at \((\bar x,\bar y+g(\bar x))\); an inverse-localization modulus may be chosen no larger than
\[
\frac{\kappa}{1-\kappa\lambda}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong metric regularity survives a smooth perturbation whose local Lipschitz size is smaller than the reciprocal regularity modulus.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is strongly metrically regular at }(\bar x,\bar y)\text{ with modulus }\kappa
g\text{ is }C^1\text{ and locally Lipschitz with modulus }\lambda
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F+g\text{ is strongly metrically regular with modulus at most }\kappa/(1-\kappa\lambda)

notation.meaning: Pointwise sum mapping with values F(x)+g(x).
Lipschitz modulus of the localized inverse of F.
Local Lipschitz modulus of the perturbation.

children.title: Regularity Under Generalized-Derivative Approximation
children.top_down_role: Persistence of solvability when exact derivative families are replaced by approximations.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularity Under Generalized-Derivative Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform invertibility persists under sufficiently accurate matrix-family approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n\geq1\), let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(U\) be a neighborhood of \(\bar x\). For every \(x\in U\), let \(\mathcal D(x)\) and \(\widetilde{\mathcal D}(x)\) be nonempty subsets of \(\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\). Suppose every \(A\in\mathcal D(x)\) is nonsingular and
\[
\sup_{x\in U}\sup_{A\in\mathcal D(x)}\|A^{-1}\|\leq\kappa.
\]
Assume that, for every \(x\in U\) and \(B\in\widetilde{\mathcal D}(x)\), there exists \(A\in\mathcal D(x)\) satisfying \(\|B-A\|\leq\varepsilon\), where \(\kappa\varepsilon<1\). Then every such \(B\) is nonsingular and
\[
\|B^{-1}\|\leq\frac{\kappa}{1-\kappa\varepsilon}.
\]
Consequently, every approximate Newton equation \(Bd=-F(x)\) has a unique solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniformly invertible family of square generalized-derivative matrices remains uniformly invertible when each approximate matrix is sufficiently close to an exact matrix; the corresponding approximate Newton equation then has a unique solution.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal D(x),\widetilde{\mathcal D}(x)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\text{ are nonempty for }x\in U
\forall x\in U\ \forall B\in\widetilde{\mathcal D}(x)\ \exists A\in\mathcal D(x):\|B-A\|\leq\varepsilon
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B\text{ is nonsingular and }\|B^{-1}\|\leq\kappa/(1-\kappa\varepsilon)

notation.meaning: Neighborhood on which the uniform bounds hold.
