children.title: Linear Newton Approximation Schemes
children.top_down_role: Unified point-dependent linear models classified by approximation and solvability properties.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Composition rule for linear Newton approximation schemes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chain rule for ordinary and strong linear Newton approximation schemes of locally Lipschitz maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be locally Lipschitz and satisfy \(G=A\circ B\), where \(B:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(A:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}^n\) are locally Lipschitz. Suppose \(T_A\) and \(T_B\) are linear Newton approximation schemes for \(A\) at \(B(\bar x)\) and for \(B\) at \(\bar x\), respectively. Then \[T(x):=\{VW:V\in T_A(B(x)),\ W\in T_B(x)\}\] is a linear Newton approximation scheme for \(G\) at \(\bar x\). If both component schemes are strong, then \(T\) is strong.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a locally Lipschitz composition, products of matrices selected from the outer and inner linear Newton approximation schemes form a scheme for the composite. Strong component schemes produce a strong composite scheme.
assumptions_latex: \(T_A\) is a linear Newton approximation scheme for \(A\) at \(B(\bar x)\)
\(T_B\) is a linear Newton approximation scheme for \(B\) at \(\bar x\)
For the strong conclusion, both \(T_A\) and \(T_B\) are strong
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T(x)=\{VW:V\in T_A(B(x)),\ W\in T_B(x)\}\) is a linear Newton approximation scheme for \(A\circ B\) at \(\bar x\), and it is strong when both component schemes are strong.

children.title: Single-Selection Linearizations
children.top_down_role: Local models formed from one admissible generalized derivative selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Selection Linearizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine Newton model generated by one admissible generalized derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) and let \(\mathcal D F(x)\subset\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) be a nonempty generalized-derivative family. A single-selection linearization at \(x\) chooses one matrix \(A_x\in\mathcal D F(x)\) and defines the affine local model
\[
M_x(h):=F(x)+A_xh.
\]
When \(m=n\) and \(A_x\) is nonsingular, its Newton correction is the unique vector \(d_x=-A_x^{-1}F(x)\), equivalently \(M_x(d_x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single-selection model chooses one matrix from an admissible generalized-derivative family and forms the corresponding affine model; if the selected matrix is square and nonsingular, the affine equation determines a unique Newton correction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_x(h)=F(x)+A_xh;\quad d_x=-A_x^{-1}F(x)\text{ when }A_x\text{ is square and nonsingular}

notation.meaning: Newton correction obtained from the selected model.

children.title: Set-Valued Linearization Families
children.top_down_role: Local approximation families analyzed uniformly over multiple selections.

knowledge_statements.title: Set-Valued Linearization Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine models indexed by every admissible generalized-derivative selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) and let \(\mathcal D F(x)\subset\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) be nonempty. The set-valued linearization family at \(x\) is
\[
\mathcal M_x(h):=\{F(x)+Ah:A\in\mathcal D F(x)\}.
\]
A quality estimate is uniform over this family when it holds for every \(A\in\mathcal D F(x)\) with constants independent of \(A\). In the square case, a uniformly regular family additionally satisfies \(A\) nonsingular and \(\sup_{A\in\mathcal D F(x)}\|A^{-1}\|<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set-valued linearization retains every affine model generated by an admissible matrix selection. Model-quality estimates may be imposed uniformly over the selections, and square families are uniformly regular when all selections are nonsingular with uniformly bounded inverses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal M_x(h)=\{F(x)+Ah:A\in\mathcal D F(x)\}

notation.meaning: Set of affine model values at displacement h.

children.title: First-Order Linearization Quality
children.top_down_role: Approximation regimes associated with linear and superlinear local behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Linearization Quality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform first-order remainder conditions determining linear or superlinear Newton behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(F(\bar x)=0\), and let \(\mathcal D F(x)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be nonempty for \(x\) near \(\bar x\). The linearizations have first-order quality with constant \(\eta\geq0\) if, for every nearby \(x\) and every admissible \(A_x\in\mathcal D F(x)\),
\[
\|F(\bar x)-F(x)-A_x(\bar x-x)\|\leq\eta\|x-\bar x\|.
\]
If each \(A_x\) is nonsingular with \(\|A_x^{-1}\|\leq\kappa\), and \(x^+\) satisfies \(F(x)+A_x(x^+-x)=0\), then
\[
\|x^+-\bar x\|\leq\kappa\eta\|x-\bar x\|.
\]
This is a contraction when \(\kappa\eta<1\). If the uniform remainder is instead \(o(\|x-\bar x\|)\) as \(x\to\bar x\), then \(\|x^+-\bar x\|/\|x-\bar x\|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform linear remainder bound yields a corresponding linear Newton error bound and becomes a contraction when the product of the inverse and remainder constants is below one. A uniform little-o remainder yields a superlinear error ratio.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|x^+-\bar x\|\leq\kappa\eta\|x-\bar x\|;\quad o(\|x-\bar x\|)\text{ remainder implies }\|x^+-\bar x\|/\|x-\bar x\|\to0

notation.meaning: Selected generalized derivative at the current point.

children.title: Higher-Order Linearization Quality
children.top_down_role: Stronger approximation regimes associated with quadratic and higher-order behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Order Linearization Quality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hölder-order model remainder producing superlinear or quadratic Newton error bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(F(\bar x)=0\), and let \(\mathcal D F(x)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be nonempty for \(x\) near \(\bar x\). Suppose every \(A_x\in\mathcal D F(x)\) is nonsingular and satisfies \(\|A_x^{-1}\|\leq\kappa\), uniformly over nearby \(x\) and all selections. The linearizations have order \(1+\alpha\), where \(0<\alpha\leq1\), if there is \(C>0\) such that
\[
\|F(\bar x)-F(x)-A_x(\bar x-x)\|\leq C\|x-\bar x\|^{1+\alpha}
\]
for every nearby \(x\) and every \(A_x\in\mathcal D F(x)\). If \(x^+\) satisfies \(F(x)+A_x(x^+-x)=0\), then
\[
\|x^+-\bar x\|\leq\kappa C\|x-\bar x\|^{1+\alpha}.
\]
The case \(\alpha=1\) gives a quadratic error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A remainder bound of order one plus alpha, uniform over nearby points and admissible matrix selections, yields a Newton error bound of the same order under uniformly bounded inverses. Alpha equal to one gives quadratic behavior.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal D F(x)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\text{ is nonempty near }\bar x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|x^+-\bar x\|\leq\kappa C\|x-\bar x\|^{1+\alpha}

notation.meaning: Hölder excess order of the model remainder.

children.title: Clarke-Jacobian Newton Methods
children.top_down_role: Newton models based on selections from convexified generalized Jacobians.

knowledge_statements.title: Clarke-Jacobian Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton iteration using arbitrary nonsingular Clarke generalized-Jacobian selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a locally Lipschitz mapping \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), an initial point \(x_0\), and tolerance \(\tau\geq0\), repeat while \(\|F(x_k)\|>\tau\): choose a nonsingular \(A_k\in\partial_C F(x_k)\), solve
\[
A_kd_k=-F(x_k),
\]
and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\). Output the first iterate satisfying the tolerance. If \(F\) is semismooth at a root \(\bar x\) and all nearby Clarke selections have uniformly bounded inverses, the iteration is locally superlinear; strong semismoothness gives a quadratic error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iterate, select a nonsingular Clarke generalized Jacobian, solve its linear Newton equation, and update; semismoothness controls the local rate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A_kd_k=-F(x_k),\quad x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k

notation.meaning: Clarke generalized Jacobian of F at x.

children.title: B-Differentiable Newton Methods
children.top_down_role: Newton models built from Bouligand derivatives and active smooth pieces.

knowledge_statements.title: B-Differentiable Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton iteration based on the Bouligand directional derivative equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be Bouligand differentiable near a root, with positively homogeneous derivative \(F'(x;\cdot)\). Given \(x_0\) and tolerance \(\tau\geq0\), repeat while \(\|F(x_k)\|>\tau\): find a correction \(d_k\) satisfying
\[
F(x_k)+F'(x_k;d_k)=0,
\]
and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\). For a piecewise-\(C^1\) mapping, one may realize the directional model using a smooth piece active along \(d_k\). Output the first iterate meeting the residual tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The B-differentiable Newton step zeros the positively homogeneous Bouligand model, optionally using a smooth piece active in the step direction.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is Bouligand differentiable near the root}
F'(x_k;\cdot)\text{ admits a solution of the model equation}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(x_k)+F'(x_k;d_k)=0,\quad x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k

notation.meaning: Bouligand directional derivative of F at x in direction d.

children.title: Newton-Derivative Methods
children.top_down_role: Methods organized around direct Newton differentiability.

knowledge_statements.title: Newton-Derivative Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton iteration using a directly specified Newton derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A mapping \(G\) is a Newton derivative of \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) near \(\bar x\) if
\[
\frac{\|F(x+h)-F(x)-G(x+h)h\|}{\|h\|}\to0
\]
as \(h\to0\), uniformly for \(x\) near \(\bar x\) when uniform analysis is required. Given \(x_0\) and \(\tau\geq0\), while \(\|F(x_k)\|>\tau\), solve \(G(x_k)d_k=-F(x_k)\) and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\). If nearby \(G(x)^{-1}\) are uniformly bounded and \(x_0\) is sufficiently close to a root, the convergence is superlinear.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Newton derivative supplies matrices with a little-o linearization residual; solving their Newton equations gives locally superlinear convergence under uniform inverse bounds.
assumptions_latex: G\text{ satisfies the Newton-derivative remainder condition}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G(x_k)d_k=-F(x_k),\quad x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k,\quad \|x_{k+1}-\bar x\|/\|x_k-\bar x\|\to0

children.title: Slant-Newton Methods
children.top_down_role: Methods based on slanting-function local models.

knowledge_statements.title: Slant-Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional slanting-function iteration for a locally Lipschitz square system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be open, let \(F:U\to\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(G:U\to\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) satisfy, for every \(x\in U\),
\[
\frac{\|F(x+h)-F(x)-G(x+h)h\|}{\|h\|}\to0
\quad\text{as }h\to0\text{ with }x+h\in U.
\]
Given \(x_0\in U\), at iteration \(k\) choose \(G_k=G(x_k)\), solve
\[
G_kd_k=-F(x_k),
\]
and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\) when \(x_{k+1}\in U\). Stop when \(F(x_k)=0\) or a prescribed residual or step tolerance holds; report failure when the selected linear system has no accepted solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iterate, use the slanting-function matrix, solve the corresponding square Newton system, and add the resulting correction.
assumptions_latex: \(U\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is open and \(F:U\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is locally Lipschitz.
\(G:U\to\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) satisfies the displayed slanting approximation at every \(x\in U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k-G(x_k)^{-1}F(x_k)\) whenever \(G(x_k)\) is nonsingular and the new iterate belongs to \(U\).

notation.meaning: slanting function assigning local model matrices

children.title: Standard Semismooth Newton Methods
children.top_down_role: Baseline semismooth Newton realizations for square residual systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Standard Semismooth Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Baseline Clarke-generalized-Jacobian Newton iteration for square semismooth equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be locally Lipschitz and semismooth, and seek \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \(F(x)=0\). Given \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), at iteration \(k\) choose \(V_k\in\partial_C F(x_k)\), solve
\[
V_kd_k=-F(x_k),
\]
and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\). Stop when the residual or step meets its prescribed tolerance; reject a selection for which the linear system has no accepted solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a matrix from the Clarke generalized Jacobian, solve the associated Newton equation, and update the iterate.
assumptions_latex: A matrix \(V_k\in\partial_C F(x_k)\) yielding an accepted linear solve can be selected at each completed iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\), where \(V_kd_k=-F(x_k)\) and \(V_k\in\partial_C F(x_k)\).

notation.meaning: Clarke generalized Jacobian of F at x

children.title: Strong-Semismooth Newton Methods
children.top_down_role: Realizations exploiting strong semismoothness and higher-quality local models.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Semismooth Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local quadratic convergence of Clarke-generalized-Jacobian Newton steps under strong semismoothness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be strongly semismooth in a neighborhood of \(x^*\in\mathbb{R}^n\), with \(F(x^*)=0\). Suppose there are a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x^*\) and a constant \(M>0\) such that every \(V\in\partial_C F(x)\), for every \(x\in U\), is nonsingular and satisfies \(\|V^{-1}\|\leq M\). For \(x_0\) sufficiently close to \(x^*\), choose any \(V_k\in\partial_C F(x_k)\), solve \(V_kd_k=-F(x_k)\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\). Then the iteration is well defined locally and
\[
\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|=O\!\left(\|x_k-x^*\|^2\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong semismoothness and uniform invertibility of all nearby Clarke generalized Jacobians give local quadratic convergence of the semismooth Newton iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is strongly semismooth near a root \(x^*\).
There exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x^*\) and \(M>0\) such that \(V\in\partial_C F(x)\) implies that \(V\) is nonsingular and \(\|V^{-1}\|\leq M\) for every \(x\in U\).

notation.meaning: Clarke generalized Jacobian of F at x
uniform bound on inverses of nearby generalized Jacobians

children.title: SC1 Newton Methods
children.top_down_role: Newton realizations for smooth maps with semismooth derivative mappings.

knowledge_statements.title: SC1 Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized-Hessian Newton iteration for a continuously differentiable map with semismooth derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable, with semismooth gradient \(g=\nabla f\), and seek a stationary point satisfying \(g(x)=0\). Given \(x_0\), select
\[
H_k\in\partial g(x_k),
\]
solve \(H_kd_k=-g(x_k)\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\). Stop when \(\|g(x_k)\|\) or \(\|d_k\|\) reaches its prescribed tolerance. The step is accepted only when the selected generalized Hessian system admits the required solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply semismooth Newton to the gradient equation, using a generalized Hessian selected from the gradient's generalized Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\), where \(H_k\in\partial g(x_k)\) and \(H_kd_k=-g(x_k)\).

children.title: Primal-Dual Active-Set Realizations
children.top_down_role: Active-set realizations structurally equivalent to selected semismooth Newton models.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Active-Set Realizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complementarity-based equivalence between an active-set solve and a semismooth Newton step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(F(x)=0\) containing a componentwise complementarity reformulation \(\phi(a_i(x),b_i(x))=0\), where \(\phi\) is piecewise smooth. At iterate \(x_k\), fix an active-set partition selecting one smooth branch of every complementarity component. Let \(V_k\) be the Jacobian of the resulting branch residual. Solving the primal-dual active-set equations for that fixed partition is exactly the linear system
\[
V_kd_k=-F(x_k),
\]
for the corresponding admissible generalized-Jacobian element \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\). Updating the active set after \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\) therefore realizes a semismooth Newton iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed complementarity branch, the primal-dual active-set linear solve equals a semismooth Newton step using the branch Jacobian.
assumptions_latex: The residual is formed from componentwise piecewise-smooth complementarity equations.
The active-set partition uniquely specifies a smooth residual branch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The active-set correction equals the semismooth Newton correction determined by the corresponding \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\).

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the branch selected by the active set

children.title: Generalized-Equation Newton Methods
children.top_down_role: Newton frameworks retaining or locally approximating the multifunction component of a generalized equation.

children.title: Josephy Newton Methods
children.top_down_role: Partial linearization methods retaining the original multifunction component.

knowledge_statements.title: Josephy Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partial linearization for a smooth mapping plus an unchanged multifunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the generalized equation
\[
0\in f(x)+Q(x),
\]
let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be continuously differentiable and \(Q:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\). Given \(x_k\), compute \(x_{k+1}\) as any solution of
\[
0\in f(x_k)+f'(x_k)(x_{k+1}-x_k)+Q(x_{k+1}).
\]
Thus only the smooth component is linearized, while the original multifunction is retained at the new point. Stop when the original inclusion is satisfied to the prescribed tolerance; report failure if the linearized generalized equation has no accepted solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearize only the smooth part of a generalized equation and solve the resulting inclusion while retaining the original multifunction at the new point.

notation.meaning: set-valued component of the generalized equation
derivative of the smooth component at the current iterate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The partial-linearization formula is the standard Josephy form and fits the algorithm leaf, but the record contains no citation or inspectable locator.

children.title: Normal-Map Newton Methods
children.top_down_role: Newton realizations based on localized normal-map equations.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Map Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal-map reduction and generalized Newton iteration for a variational inequality over a closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be locally Lipschitz, and consider
\[
0\in f(x)+N_C(x).
\]
Define the normal map \(F_C:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) by
\[
F_C(z)=f(\Pi_C z)+z-\Pi_C z.
\]
Given \(z_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), choose \(V_k\in\partial_C F_C(z_k)\), solve \(V_kd_k=-F_C(z_k)\), and set \(z_{k+1}=z_k+d_k\). The associated primal iterate is \(x_{k+1}=\Pi_Cz_{k+1}\). Stop when \(\|F_C(z_k)\|\) reaches its prescribed tolerance; reject a selection for which the linear system has no accepted solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convert the normal-cone inclusion to its normal-map equation, apply a Clarke-generalized-Jacobian Newton step in the normal variable, and project the updated point to the primal variable.

notation.meaning: Clarke generalized Jacobian of the normal map

children.title: Semismooth-Star Newton Methods
children.top_down_role: Coderivative-oriented Newton methods for generalized equations.

knowledge_statements.title: Semismooth-Star Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coderivative Newton step for a set-valued generalized equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^n\), and seek \(x\) with \(0\in F(x)\). At iteration \(k\), choose a nearby graph point \((\hat x_k,\hat y_k)\in\operatorname{gph}F\) and coderivative pairs
\[
(v_i,u_i)\in\operatorname{gph}D^*F(\hat x_k,\hat y_k),\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.
\]
Form matrices \(A_k\) and \(B_k\) with rows \(u_i^\top\) and \(v_i^\top\), respectively, solve
\[
A_kd_k=-B_k\hat y_k,
\]
and set \(x_{k+1}=\hat x_k+d_k\). Stop when the graph residual meets its prescribed tolerance; reject singular model selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select coderivative pairs at a nearby graph point, solve their square Newton model, and correct the graph-point primal coordinate.
assumptions_latex: The selected coderivative rows produce a solvable square model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=\hat x_k+d_k\), where \(A_kd_k=-B_k\hat y_k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The precise placement of coderivative components in A_k and B_k and the equation A_k d_k=-B_k y_k are convention-sensitive. No source is supplied to validate this semismooth-star realization.

children.title: SCD Semismooth-Star Methods
children.top_down_role: Subspace-containing-derivative realizations of semismooth-star Newton models.

knowledge_statements.title: SCD Semismooth-Star Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semismooth-star Newton realization using subspaces supplied by an SCD mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^n\), and seek \(0\in F(x)\). At iteration \(k\), select \((\hat x_k,\hat y_k)\in\operatorname{gph}F\) and an admissible \(n\)-dimensional subspace from the subspace-containing derivative of \(F\), represented by matrices \((A_k,B_k)\) through
\[
L_k=\{(B_k^\top p,A_k^\top p):p\in\mathbb{R}^n\}.
\]
If \(A_k\) is nonsingular, solve \(A_kd_k=-B_k\hat y_k\) and set \(x_{k+1}=\hat x_k+d_k\). Stop at the prescribed graph-residual tolerance; otherwise reject the selected subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent an admissible SCD subspace by two matrices, solve its Newton correction equation, and update the primal graph coordinate.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^n\) admits the stated SCD subspace selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=\hat x_k-A_k^{-1}B_k\hat y_k\).

notation.meaning: matrix representation of the selected subspace

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and orientation of the SCD subspace representation, the required nonsingularity block, and the resulting Newton equation all require an authoritative source. None is supplied.

children.title: Inexact Nonsmooth Newton Methods
children.top_down_role: Newton models with controlled local-system solution inaccuracies.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Nonsmooth Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-controlled inexact solution of generalized-Jacobian Newton systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be locally Lipschitz. Given \(x_0\) and forcing terms \(\eta_k\in[0,1)\), choose \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\) and compute \(d_k\) with linear residual \(r_k\) satisfying
\[
V_kd_k=-F(x_k)+r_k,\qquad \|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|.
\]
Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\). Stop when the nonlinear residual or step meets its prescribed tolerance. The forcing sequence controls the permitted local-system error; choosing \(\eta_k=0\) recovers the exact generalized Newton step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve each generalized Newton system only approximately, bounding its linear residual by a forcing fraction of the current nonlinear residual.
assumptions_latex: \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\) and \(0\leq\eta_k<1\) are selected at each iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\) with \(\|V_kd_k+F(x_k)\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\).

notation.meaning: residual of the inexact linear solve
forcing term controlling relative linear-solve accuracy

children.title: Quasi-Newton Models
children.top_down_role: Derivative-surrogate local models updated from equation information.

knowledge_statements.title: Quasi-Newton Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine local residual models whose matrices approximate derivative information without recomputing an exact derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) approximate local derivative information for \(F\) at \(x_k\). The associated quasi-Newton model is
\[
m_k(x)=F(x_k)+B_k(x-x_k).
\]
When \(B_k\) is nonsingular, the zero of this affine model is \(x_k+d_k\), where
\[
B_kd_k=-F(x_k).
\]
The matrix \(B_k\) may be updated from sampled iterate and residual differences; a common one-pair update enforces \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\), where \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\) and \(y_k=F(x_{k+1})-F(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quasi-Newton model replaces the exact local derivative by an approximate matrix in an affine residual model; when invertible, that model determines a Newton-like correction. Secant interpolation is one common way to update the matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) can be evaluated at the sampled points.
\(B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is an approximate local derivative matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_k(x)=F(x_k)+B_k(x-x_k)\), and if \(B_k\) is nonsingular its model-zero correction satisfies \(B_kd_k=-F(x_k)\).

notation.meaning: iterate and residual differences used by a secant update

children.title: Secant Models
children.top_down_role: Local surrogate models constrained by individual secant relationships.

knowledge_statements.title: Secant Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-pair interpolation condition for a linear residual model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(x_{k-1}\neq x_k\). Define
\[
s_{k-1}=x_k-x_{k-1},\qquad y_{k-1}=F(x_k)-F(x_{k-1}).
\]
A matrix \(B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is a secant model for this pair when
\[
B_ks_{k-1}=y_{k-1}.
\]
Equivalently, the affine model \(m_k(x)=F(x_k)+B_k(x-x_k)\) interpolates both sampled residuals: \(m_k(x_k)=F(x_k)\) and \(m_k(x_{k-1})=F(x_{k-1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A secant matrix maps the latest iterate difference to the corresponding residual difference, so its affine model interpolates both sampled residuals.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is evaluated at distinct points \(x_{k-1}\) and \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_ks_{k-1}=y_{k-1}\), equivalently \(m_k(x_j)=F(x_j)\) for \(j\in\{k-1,k\}\).

notation.meaning: affine secant model anchored at the current iterate

knowledge_statements.title: Multisecant Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear local surrogates satisfying several stored secant equations simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and retain displacement pairs \(s_i=x_i^+-x_i\) and \(y_i=F(x_i^+)-F(x_i)\) for \(i=1,\ldots,p\). Write \(S=[s_1\ \cdots\ s_p]\) and \(Y=[y_1\ \cdots\ y_p]\). A multisecant local model at \(x\) is \(M_x(d)=F(x)+Bd\), where \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) satisfies \(BS=Y\). If this system is inconsistent, a regularized multisecant model selects \(B\) by minimizing \(\|BS-Y\|_F^2+\mu\|B-B_0\|_F^2\) for prescribed \(\mu>0\) and reference matrix \(B_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multisecant model uses one matrix to interpolate several stored changes in the residual; regularization resolves incompatible or underdetermined secant equations.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is defined at every stored pair endpoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_x(d)=F(x)+Bd\) with \(BS=Y\), or with \(B\) given by the stated regularized least-squares problem.

notation.meaning: Matrices of stored displacements and residual differences.

children.title: Surrogate Consistency
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of derivative surrogates with local nonsmooth equation behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order consistency of a local surrogate along trial or accepted displacements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), base points \(x_k\), nonzero displacements \(d_k\to0\), and local surrogates \(M_k\) satisfying \(M_k(0)=F(x_k)\), the surrogates are first-order consistent along \((x_k,d_k)\) when \[\frac{\|F(x_k+d_k)-M_k(d_k)\|}{\|d_k\|}\longrightarrow0.\] They are uniformly first-order consistent on a set \(X\) if \[\sup_{x\in X}\sup_{0<\|d\|\leq t}\frac{\|F(x+d)-M_x(d)\|}{\|d\|}\longrightarrow0\quad\text{as }t\downarrow0,\] whenever the displayed points belong to the domain of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A surrogate is consistent when its prediction error is little-o of the displacement, along the modeled steps or uniformly over nearby admissible steps.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) and every evaluated point lies in \(\operatorname{dom}F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|F(x_k+d_k)-M_k(d_k)\|=o(\|d_k\|)\), with the displayed supremum criterion for uniform consistency.

notation.meaning: Local surrogate based at the point x_k.

children.title: Regularized Newton Models
children.top_down_role: Local models stabilized against singular or unreliable generalized derivatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Newton Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tikhonov-stabilized linearized residual models for possibly singular generalized derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), choose a local derivative surrogate \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) at \(x\), and let \(\lambda>0\). The regularized Newton model selects the unique step \[d_\lambda=\operatorname*{argmin}_{d\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{\frac12\|F(x)+Ad\|^2+\frac{\lambda}{2}\|d\|^2\right\}.\] Equivalently, \(d_\lambda\) is the unique solution of \[(A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda I)d_\lambda=-A^{\mathsf T}F(x).\] The positive regularization makes the normal-equation matrix positive definite even when \(A\) is rectangular or rank deficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The model adds a positive quadratic penalty to the linearized residual, producing a unique stable step despite singular or unreliable derivative information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_\lambda=-(A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda I)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}F(x)\) is uniquely defined.

children.title: Least-Squares Local Models
children.top_down_role: Residual-minimizing local models for inconsistent or overdetermined linearizations.

knowledge_statements.title: Least-Squares Local Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-minimizing Newton models for rectangular or inconsistent linearizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(F(x)\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and a local derivative surrogate \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), a least-squares local Newton step is any \[d_{\mathrm{LS}}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{d\in\mathbb{R}^n}\|F(x)+Ad\|^2.\] Such a step exists and is characterized by the normal equations \[A^{\mathsf T}(F(x)+Ad_{\mathrm{LS}})=0.\] Hence its linearized residual is orthogonal to \(\operatorname{range}A\). The minimizing step is unique exactly when \(A\) has full column rank; otherwise the set of minimizers is an affine translate of \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A least-squares local model chooses a step minimizing the linearized residual; uniqueness holds precisely when the surrogate matrix has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^{\mathsf T}(F(x)+Ad_{\mathrm{LS}})=0\), with uniqueness if and only if \(\ker A=\{0\}\).

children.title: Minimum-Norm Local Models
children.top_down_role: Norm-selecting local models for underdetermined or nonunique linearizations.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Norm Local Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical shortest steps for underdetermined exact or least-squares linearizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(F(x)\in\mathbb{R}^m\), the minimum-norm local step is the unique vector \[d_\star=\operatorname*{argmin}\left\{\|d\|:d\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in\mathbb{R}^n}\|F(x)+Au\|\right\}.\] It is given by \[d_\star=-A^\dagger F(x),\] where \(A^\dagger\) is the Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse. If the exact linearized equation \(Ad=-F(x)\) is consistent, this is equivalently its unique minimum-norm solution. Moreover, \(d_\star\in\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})=(\ker A)^\perp\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among all least-squares steps, the pseudoinverse step is uniquely shortest and lies orthogonally to the matrix nullspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_\star=-A^\dagger F(x)\in(\ker A)^\perp\) is the unique minimum-norm least-squares step.

children.title: Rectangular-System Geometry
children.top_down_role: Local equation geometry when residual and variable dimensions differ.

knowledge_statements.title: Rectangular-System Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal decompositions governing residual and step selection for rectangular linearizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b=-F(x)\). Every vector admits the orthogonal decompositions \[\mathbb{R}^m=\operatorname{range}A\oplus\ker A^{\mathsf T},\qquad \mathbb{R}^n=\operatorname{range}A^{\mathsf T}\oplus\ker A.\] For any least-squares solution \(d\), the residual \(r=Ad-b\) belongs to \(\ker A^{\mathsf T}\), while all least-squares solutions have the same component in \(\operatorname{range}A^{\mathsf T}\). Adding a vector from \(\ker A\) leaves the residual unchanged. Consequently, the unique minimum-norm least-squares solution is the solution lying in \(\operatorname{range}A^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rectangular systems split residual space and step space orthogonally; nullspace motion preserves the residual, and removing it yields the shortest step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ad-b\in\ker A^{\mathsf T}\), and the minimum-norm minimizer belongs to \(\operatorname{range}A^{\mathsf T}\).

children.title: Rank-Deficient Solution Selection
children.top_down_role: Selection among local corrections when the linearized model lacks full rank.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Solution Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pseudoinverse parameterization and canonical selection among nonunique linearized steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) be rank deficient and let \(b=-F(x)\). The complete set of least-squares solutions of \(Ad\approx b\) is \[\left\{A^\dagger b+(I-A^\dagger A)z:z\in\mathbb{R}^n\right\}.\] Here \(I-A^\dagger A\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker A\). The canonical minimum-norm selection is \(d_\star=A^\dagger b=-A^\dagger F(x)\). It is also the limit \[d_\star=\lim_{\lambda\downarrow0}(A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda I)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}b.\] Thus pseudoinverse selection removes precisely the undetermined nullspace component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All rank-deficient least-squares steps equal the pseudoinverse step plus arbitrary nullspace motion; choosing zero nullspace motion gives the unique shortest step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d=A^\dagger b+(I-A^\dagger A)z\), and \(d_\star=A^\dagger b\) is the unique minimum-norm selection.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the nullspace of A.

children.title: Active-Set Matrix Assembly
children.top_down_role: Construction of local matrices from complementarity or bound-activity states.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Matrix Assembly
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rowwise assembly for componentwise maxima of finitely many smooth pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_i(x)=\max_{j\in J_i}f_{ij}(x)\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), where every \(f_{ij}\) is continuously differentiable near \(x\). Compute \(I_i(x)=\{j\in J_i:f_{ij}(x)=F_i(x)\}\), select \(\alpha_i\in I_i(x)\), and assemble \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) rowwise by \[A_{i:}=\nabla f_{i\alpha_i}(x)^{\mathsf T}.\] Use \(F(x)+Ad\) as the local model and solve the chosen Newton, least-squares, or regularized subproblem. The output is the selected active-pattern matrix \(A\) together with its pattern \((\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identify an active smooth piece in each max component, place its gradient in the corresponding matrix row, and use the assembled matrix locally.
assumptions_latex: \(J_i\) is finite and nonempty for each \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_{i:}=\nabla f_{i\alpha_i}(x)^{\mathsf T}\) for a selected \(\alpha_i\in I_i(x)\).

notation.meaning: Active piece indices for component i at x.
Row i of the assembled matrix.

children.title: Smooth-Piece Matrix Assembly
children.top_down_role: Construction of local matrices from selected smooth residual pieces.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth-Piece Matrix Assembly
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Jacobian assembly from a locally active smooth selection of a piecewise-smooth mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a continuous mapping \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) has finitely many continuously differentiable selections \(F^\sigma\) on regions \(R_\sigma\), with \(F=F^\sigma\) on \(R_\sigma\). At a base point \(x\), choose an index \(\sigma\) satisfying \(x\in\overline{\operatorname{int}R_\sigma}\) and \(F(x)=F^\sigma(x)\), then assemble \[A=DF^\sigma(x).\] Use \(M_x(d)=F(x)+Ad\) as the local model. When \(DF^\sigma(x)\) is obtained as a limit from differentiability points inside \(R_\sigma\), the assembled matrix is a limiting Jacobian associated with that smooth piece.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a smooth selection whose region reaches the base point, assemble its Jacobian, and use that matrix in the local linear model.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is continuous and admits finitely many continuously differentiable local selections.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_x(d)=F(x)+DF^\sigma(x)d\) is the smooth-piece local model.

notation.meaning: Region associated with smooth selection sigma.
Jacobian of the selected smooth piece.

children.title: Tie-State Assembly
children.top_down_role: Local matrix construction when multiple activity states or smooth pieces are eligible.

knowledge_statements.title: Tie-State Assembly
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexified row assembly when several smooth pieces share the active value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F_i(x)=\max_{j\in J_i}f_{ij}(x)\), compute the tied active set \(I_i(x)=\{j:f_{ij}(x)=F_i(x)\}\). Choose weights \(\theta_{ij}\geq0\) satisfying \(\sum_{j\in I_i(x)}\theta_{ij}=1\), and assemble \[A_{i:}=\sum_{j\in I_i(x)}\theta_{ij}\nabla f_{ij}(x)^{\mathsf T}.\] A deterministic extreme selection is recovered by assigning weight one to a single tied index. The convexified row belongs to the Clarke subdifferential of the scalar component \(F_i\); the completed matrix is the output tie-state model used in the local linearization \(F(x)+Ad\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a tie, form each model row from a convex combination of gradients of all tied smooth pieces, or choose an extreme tied piece.
assumptions_latex: \(J_i\) is finite and every \(f_{ij}\) is continuously differentiable near \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_{i:}\in\operatorname{conv}\{\nabla f_{ij}(x)^{\mathsf T}:j\in I_i(x)\}\).

notation.meaning: Tied active indices of component i.

children.title: Active-Pattern Instability
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of assembled models to small changes in the detected active pattern.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Pattern Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discontinuous active-piece selection at ties despite continuity of the underlying residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(F:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}\) defined by \(F(x_1,x_2)=\max\{x_1,x_2\}\). Away from the tie line \(x_1=x_2\), active-piece assembly gives \(A=[1\ 0]\) when \(x_1>x_2\) and \(A=[0\ 1]\) when \(x_2>x_1\). For \(x^k=(1/k,0)\) and \(y^k=(0,1/k)\), both sequences converge to \((0,0)\), but their assembled matrices remain different. Thus a single-valued extreme active-pattern rule need not be continuous at a tie, and arbitrarily small perturbations can switch the local Newton matrix by a nonvanishing amount.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a max function, points approaching the same tie from opposite sides select different gradients, so extreme active-pattern matrices can jump discontinuously.
assumptions_latex: Assembly selects the uniquely active smooth piece away from ties.

notation.meaning: Sequences approaching the tie from opposite active regions.

children.title: Coherent Block Assembly
children.top_down_role: Assembly preserving shared selections across primal, dual, and complementarity blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Coherent Block Assembly
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shared piece selection across coupled primal, dual, and complementarity residual blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a block residual \(R=(R_1,\ldots,R_q)\) possess common smooth selections \(R^\sigma=(R_1^\sigma,\ldots,R_q^\sigma)\) indexed by \(\sigma\in\Sigma\). A block matrix \(A\) assembled at \(z\) is coherent when there exist active indices \(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_p\) and common weights \(\theta_\ell\geq0\), with \(\sum_{\ell=1}^p\theta_\ell=1\), such that every block row uses the same selections and weights: \[A_{r:}=\sum_{\ell=1}^p\theta_\ell DR_r^{\sigma_\ell}(z),\qquad r=1,\ldots,q.\] Equivalently, \(A=\sum_{\ell=1}^p\theta_\ell DR^{\sigma_\ell}(z)\). Independent blockwise mixtures that admit no such common representation are incoherent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block assembly is coherent when every coupled residual block uses the same active selections and convex weights, yielding one joint generalized matrix.
assumptions_latex: Each selected \(\sigma_\ell\) is active at \(z\), and \(\theta\) lies in the probability simplex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A=\sum_{\ell=1}^p\theta_\ell DR^{\sigma_\ell}(z)\) with the same \(\sigma_\ell\) and \(\theta_\ell\) in every block.

notation.meaning: Shared convex weight across all blocks.

children.title: Matrix-Free Generalized-Derivative Actions
children.top_down_role: Evaluation of generalized linear models through operator actions.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free Generalized-Derivative Actions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Krylov realization of a selected generalized Newton model without forming its matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given locally Lipschitz \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), an iterate \(x_k\), and a selected \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\), suppose an oracle returns \(v\mapsto V_kv\). Apply a matrix-free linear solver to \(V_kd=-F(x_k)\), using only oracle products and residual evaluations. Stop when \(\|V_kd_k+F(x_k)\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\), and output \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\). The realization is equivalent to the explicit selected model whenever the oracle computes the same linear action and the stopping rule is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select a generalized derivative and approximately solve its Newton equation using only derivative-vector products, terminating at a prescribed relative residual.
assumptions_latex: \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\) is fixed during the linear solve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|V_kd_k+F(x_k)\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\) and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\).

notation.meaning: Clarke generalized Jacobian of F at x

children.title: Rank-Deficient Model Stabilization Pipeline
children.top_down_role: Detection and local treatment of singular or nearly singular Newton models.

children.title: Rank-Deficiency Detection
children.top_down_role: Local identification of deficient rank in generalized Newton models.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficiency Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and tolerance-based detection for a square generalized Newton matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a selected model matrix \(V\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) with singular values \(\sigma_1(V)\geq\cdots\geq\sigma_n(V)\geq0\), exact rank deficiency is the predicate \(\sigma_n(V)=0\), equivalently \(\operatorname{rank}(V)<n\). Given a numerical threshold \(\tau>0\), declare numerical rank \(r_\tau=\#\{i:\sigma_i(V)>\tau\}\) and flag numerical rank deficiency precisely when \(r_\tau<n\). The thresholded predicate is scale dependent unless \(\tau\) is normalized relative to \(\sigma_1(V)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model is exactly rank deficient when its smallest singular value vanishes; numerical deficiency uses a stated singular-value threshold.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau>0\) is fixed and reported with the diagnostic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(V)<n\iff\sigma_n(V)=0\), while numerical deficiency means \(r_\tau<n\).

children.title: Near-Singularity Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Local indicators of ill-conditioned or nearly singular model matrices.

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Singularity Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-aware conditioning tests for a selected generalized Newton matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular and let \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\). Define the reciprocal spectral condition estimate \(\rho(V)=\sigma_n(V)/\sigma_1(V)=1/\kappa_2(V)\). The model is diagnosed as near singular at tolerance \(\varepsilon\) when \(\rho(V)\leq\varepsilon\). Equivalently, there exists a unit vector \(z\) satisfying \(\|Vz\|\leq\varepsilon\|V\|_2\). This diagnostic distinguishes ill-conditioning from exact rank deficiency because \(\sigma_n(V)>0\) remains possible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular model is near singular when its reciprocal condition number falls below a stated relative tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(V)\leq\varepsilon\iff\min_{\|z\|=1}\|Vz\|\leq\varepsilon\|V\|_2\).

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Model Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Levenberg–Marquardt stabilization of a singular or ill-conditioned generalized Newton model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), residual \(r=F(x)\), selected model \(V\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and \(\lambda>0\), compute the unique minimizer \[d_\lambda=\operatorname*{argmin}_{d\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{\tfrac12\|Vd+r\|^2+\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\|d\|^2\right\}.\] Equivalently, solve \((V^{\mathsf T}V+\lambda I_n)d_\lambda=-V^{\mathsf T}r\), then set \(x^+=x+d_\lambda\). Since \(V^{\mathsf T}V+\lambda I_n\) is positive definite, the stabilized step exists uniquely even when \(V\) is rank deficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a positive quadratic penalty to the local least-squares model, producing a unique step even for a rank-deficient selected derivative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_\lambda=-(V^{\mathsf T}V+\lambda I_n)^{-1}V^{\mathsf T}r\) exists uniquely.

notation.meaning: identity matrix on the step space

children.title: Null-Space-Aware Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Local treatment that accounts for detected null spaces or deficient model directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Null-Space-Aware Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stabilization that isolates and penalizes directions invisible to the selected model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(V\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(r\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and a matrix \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times q}\) whose orthonormal columns span \(\ker V\), set \(P_N=ZZ^{\mathsf T}\). For \(\lambda>0\), compute the unique vector \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \[(V^{\mathsf T}V+\lambda P_N)d=-V^{\mathsf T}r.\] The coefficient is positive definite because \(V^{\mathsf T}V\) is positive definite on \((\ker V)^\perp\) and \(\lambda P_N\) is positive definite on \(\ker V\). The resulting step satisfies \(P_Nd=0\) and equals the minimum-norm least-squares correction \(-V^\dagger r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalize only the selected derivative's null space, preserving the observable correction and selecting the minimum-norm least-squares step.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times q}\) has orthonormal columns spanning \(\ker V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d=-V^\dagger r\) and \(P_Nd=0\).

notation.meaning: orthogonal projector onto the null space of V
dimension of the null space of V

children.title: Basic Local Nonsmooth Newton Convergence Principle
children.top_down_role: The foundational convergence family linking local-model solvability, approximation quality, and neighborhood control.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Rate Regimes for Inexact Nonsmooth Newton Iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local convergence rates governed by forcing parameters and Newton-approximation strength.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G:\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), where \(\Omega\) is open. Suppose that \(G\) is locally Lipschitz near \(x^*\in\Omega\), \(G(x^*)=0\), and \(G\) admits a nonsingular Newton approximation \(\mathcal A\) at \(x^*\). There exists \(\bar\eta>0\) such that, if \(\eta_k\leq\bar\eta\) for every \(k\), then for every \(\varepsilon\in(0,\varepsilon_{\mathcal A}]\), every sufficiently close initial point yields a well-defined inexact Newton method, and every generated sequence converges Q-linearly to \(x^*\). If \(\eta_k\to0\), convergence is Q-superlinear. If, additionally, \(\mathcal A\) is strong and \(\eta_k\leq\widetilde\eta\|G(x^k)\|\) for some \(\widetilde\eta>0\) and all \(k\), convergence is Q-quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficiently small uniform forcing bound gives local Q-linear convergence of the inexact nonsmooth Newton method. Vanishing forcing parameters give Q-superlinear convergence; residual-proportional forcing together with a strong Newton approximation gives Q-quadratic convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) admits a nonsingular Newton approximation \(\mathcal A\) at \(x^*\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every generated sequence converges Q-linearly; if \(\eta_k\to0\), it converges Q-superlinearly; if \(\mathcal A\) is strong and \(\eta_k\leq\widetilde\eta\|G(x^k)\|\), it converges Q-quadratically.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Superlinear and Quadratic Convergence of the Piecewise-Smooth Newton Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A local convergence-rate specialization of the basic nonsmooth Newton principle for an active-piece Newton iteration on a PC^1 equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G:\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), with \(\Omega\) open, be a \(PC^1\) function with \(C^1\) pieces \(\{G^i:i=1,\ldots,k\}\), and let \(x^*\in\Omega\) satisfy \(G(x^*)=0\). If \(JG^i(x^*)\) is nonsingular for every \(i\in\mathcal P(x^*)\), then there exists \(\delta>0\) such that, for every \(x^0\in B(x^*,\delta)\), Algorithm 7.2.14 generates a unique sequence \(\{x^k\}\) converging Q-superlinearly to \(x^*\). If the Jacobians of all pieces active at points near \(x^*\) are locally Lipschitz at \(x^*\), then the convergence is Q-quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a piecewise-C1 equation, nonsingularity at the solution of every active piece Jacobian gives local unique generation and Q-superlinear convergence of the active-piece Newton iteration. Local Lipschitz regularity of Jacobians of pieces active nearby strengthens the rate to Q-quadratic.
assumptions_latex: JG^i(x^*)\text{ is nonsingular for every }i\in\mathcal P(x^*)
\text{For Q-quadratic convergence, the Jacobians of all pieces active at points near }x^*\text{ are locally Lipschitz at }x^*
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\delta>0\ \forall x^0\in B(x^*,\delta):\ \text{Algorithm 7.2.14 generates a unique sequence }\{x^k\}\text{ converging Q-superlinearly to }x^*;\ \text{under the additional Lipschitz-Jacobian assumption, convergence is Q-quadratic}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Superlinear and Quadratic Convergence of the Nonsmooth Newton Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local convergence under a nonsingular abstract Newton approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G:\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), where \(\Omega\) is open. Suppose that \(G\) is locally Lipschitz near \(x^*\in\Omega\), \(G(x^*)=0\), and \(G\) admits a nonsingular Newton approximation \(\mathcal A\) at \(x^*\). For every \(\varepsilon\in(0,\varepsilon_{\mathcal A}]\), there exists \(\delta>0\) such that, whenever \(x^0\in\mathbb B(x^*,\delta)\), the nonsmooth Newton algorithm generates a unique sequence \(\{x^k\}\) converging Q-superlinearly to \(x^*\). If \(\mathcal A\) is strong, the convergence is Q-quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a zero, a locally Lipschitz mapping with a nonsingular Newton approximation has a uniquely defined local nonsmooth Newton sequence that converges Q-superlinearly. A strong approximation upgrades the rate to Q-quadratic.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) admits a nonsingular Newton approximation \(\mathcal A\) at \(x^*\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Newton algorithm generates a unique sequence with \(x^k\to x^*\) Q-superlinearly; if \(\mathcal A\) is strong, convergence is Q-quadratic.

children.title: Local Well-Definedness
children.top_down_role: Existence of admissible and solvable local Newton models near a solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Well-Definedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional generalized Newton steps near an isolated zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be locally Lipschitz, let \(F(x_*)=0\), and suppose every \(V\in\partial F(x_*)\) is nonsingular. Then there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x_*\) and \(M<\infty\) such that every \(V\in\partial F(x)\), with \(x\in U\), is nonsingular and satisfies \(\|V^{-1}\|\leq M\). Consequently, for every \(x_k\in U\) and every selection \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\), the Newton equation \(V_kd_k=-F(x_k)\) has a unique solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform nonsingularity of generalized Jacobians at a zero makes every nearby selected Newton model uniquely solvable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists U,M\;\forall x\in U\;\forall V\in\partial F(x): V^{-1}\text{ exists and }\|V^{-1}\|\leq M\).

children.title: Neighborhood Invariance
children.top_down_role: Persistence of iterates within a region where local assumptions remain valid.

knowledge_statements.title: Neighborhood Invariance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant-ball criterion for retaining all local Newton assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:U\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be a locally defined Newton update with fixed point \(T(x_*)=x_*\). If a closed ball \(B_\rho(x_*)\subset U\) and a constant \(q\in[0,1)\) satisfy \(\|T(x)-x_*\|\leq q\|x-x_*\|\) for every \(x\in B_\rho(x_*)\), then \(T(B_\rho(x_*))\subseteq B_\rho(x_*)\). Hence every sequence \(x_{k+1}=T(x_k)\) starting in that ball remains there, and all assumptions asserted throughout the ball remain applicable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contractive Newton update maps a sufficiently small validity ball into itself, so every iterate retains the local assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \(\|T(x)-x_*\|\leq q\|x-x_*\|\) on the ball for some \(q<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_0\in B_\rho(x_*)\implies x_k\in B_\rho(x_*)\) for every \(k\geq0\).

notation.meaning: closed radius-rho ball around the solution

children.title: Solution-Branch Selection
children.top_down_role: Local behavior when inverse mappings or solution sets have multiple branches.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Branch Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch selection by disjoint invariant localizations around isolated solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) have distinct isolated zeros \(x_*^1,\ldots,x_*^s\), and let \(U_1,\ldots,U_s\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be pairwise disjoint, nonempty closed neighborhoods such that \(x_*^i\) is the unique zero of \(F\) in \(U_i\). A local Newton update \(T\) selects branch \(i\) if \(T(U_i)\subseteq U_i\) and \(T(x_*^i)=x_*^i\). If \(T\) is a contraction on \(U_i\), then every iteration \(x_{k+1}=T(x_k)\) initialized at \(x_0\in U_i\) remains in \(U_i\) and converges to \(x_*^i\), independently of zeros in the other localizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed invariant neighborhood containing one fixed solution selects that solution branch; contraction within the neighborhood forces convergence to it.
assumptions_latex: The sets \(U_i\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) are nonempty, closed, pairwise disjoint, and each contains exactly one zero \(x_*^i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_0\in U_i\implies x_k\in U_i\text{ for every }k\geq0\text{ and }x_k\to x_*^i\).

notation.meaning: closed invariant localization of solution branch i

children.title: Linear Local Convergence

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Local Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Q-linear convergence from a uniform local error contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_*\) be a solution and let an iteration be well defined in a neighborhood of \(x_*\). If there exist \(q\in(0,1)\), \(\rho>0\), and \(k_0\) such that every iterate with \(k\geq k_0\) lies in \(B_\rho(x_*)\) and satisfies \(\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|\leq q\|x_k-x_*\|\), then \(x_k\to x_*\) Q-linearly. In particular, \(\|x_k-x_*\|\leq q^{k-k_0}\|x_{k_0}-x_*\|\) for all \(k\geq k_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform error contraction by a factor below one yields Q-linear convergence and a geometric error bound.
assumptions_latex: The iteration is locally well defined.

children.title: Superlinear Local Convergence
children.top_down_role: Fast local behavior associated with Newton-quality and semismooth models.

knowledge_statements.title: Superlinear Local Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Q-superlinear convergence from a vanishing selected-model remainder.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(F(x_*)=0\), and let \(x_k\to x_*\), with \(x_k\neq x_*\) for all sufficiently large \(k\). For each such \(k\), choose an invertible generalized derivative \(V_k\) at \(x_k\) and define \(x_{k+1}=x_k-V_k^{-1}F(x_k)\). If \(\|V_k^{-1}\|\leq M\) uniformly and \[\|F(x_k)-F(x_*)-V_k(x_k-x_*)\|=o(\|x_k-x_*\|),\] then \[\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|}{\|x_k-x_*\|}=0.\] Hence \(x_k\) converges Q-superlinearly to \(x_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly invertible generalized Newton models whose remainders are negligible relative to the current error yield Q-superlinear convergence.
assumptions_latex: Each \(V_k\) is an invertible generalized derivative at \(x_k\), and \(\|V_k^{-1}\|\leq M\) uniformly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|}{\|x_k-x_*\|}=0\).

notation.meaning: selected invertible generalized derivative at the current iterate
quantity negligible relative to the current error
uniform bound on inverse selected models

children.title: Quadratic Local Convergence
children.top_down_role: Quadratic behavior associated with strong semismoothness and stronger model accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Local Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Q-quadratic convergence from a second-order selected-model remainder.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(F(x_*)=0\). Suppose that whenever \(x_k\in B_\rho(x_*)\), an invertible generalized derivative \(V_k\) at \(x_k\) is selected and \(x_{k+1}=x_k-V_k^{-1}F(x_k)\), with \(\|V_k^{-1}\|\leq M\) and \[\|F(x_k)-F(x_*)-V_k(x_k-x_*)\|\leq L\|x_k-x_*\|^2.\] If \(ML\rho<1\) and \(x_0\in B_\rho(x_*)\), then every iterate remains in the ball and \[\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|\leq ML\|x_k-x_*\|^2.\] Consequently, \(x_k\) converges Q-quadratically to \(x_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniformly invertible generalized Newton model with a quadratic remainder converges Q-quadratically when initialized in a sufficiently small validity ball.
assumptions_latex: For \(x_k\in B_\rho(x_*)\), \(V_k\) is invertible and \(\|V_k^{-1}\|\leq M\).
The selected-model remainder is at most \(L\|x_k-x_*\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|\leq ML\|x_k-x_*\|^2\) and \(x_k\to x_*\) Q-quadratically.

notation.meaning: selected generalized derivative at the current iterate
inverse bound and quadratic remainder constant

children.title: Order-Dependent Local Convergence
children.top_down_role: Rate families indexed by intermediate or higher-order approximation quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Order-Dependent Local Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Q-order determined by the exponent of the selected-model remainder.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be locally Lipschitz with \(F(x_*)=0\). Suppose that whenever \(x_k\in B_\rho(x_*)\), one selects an invertible \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\) and sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k-V_k^{-1}F(x_k)\). Assume \(\|V_k^{-1}\|\leq M\) and, for some \(\alpha>0\) and \(L>0\), \[\|F(x_k)-F(x_*)-V_k(x_k-x_*)\|\leq L\|x_k-x_*\|^{1+\alpha}.\] If \(ML\rho^\alpha<1\) and \(x_0\in B_\rho(x_*)\), then every iterate remains in the ball and \[\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|\leq ML\|x_k-x_*\|^{1+\alpha}.\] Consequently, \(x_k\) converges to \(x_*\) with Q-order at least \(1+\alpha\); the case \(\alpha=1\) is Q-quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A selected-model remainder of order one plus alpha gives local Q-order at least one plus alpha when the iteration starts in a sufficiently small validity ball.
assumptions_latex: \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\) is invertible and \(\|V_k^{-1}\|\leq M\) in \(B_\rho(x_*)\).
The selected-model remainder is at most \(L\|x_k-x_*\|^{1+\alpha}\) for some \(\alpha>0\) and \(L>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|\leq ML\|x_k-x_*\|^{1+\alpha}\), so the Q-order is at least \(1+\alpha\).

notation.meaning: selected Clarke generalized Jacobian at the current iterate

children.title: B-Newton Convergence Family

Then, for every sufficiently close initial point \(x_0\), the iterates are well defined, remain near \(\bar x\), and converge to \(\bar x\). assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is locally Lipschitz and semismooth at a root \(\bar x\).
Every \(V\in\partial F(x)\) is nonsingular near \(\bar x\), with \(\|V^{-1}\|\le M\).
For quadratic convergence, \(F\) is strongly semismooth: the model remainder is \(O(\|h\|^2)\).

children.title: Josephy-Newton Convergence Family
children.top_down_role: Local convergence based on strong regularity of generalized-equation linearizations.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\), and \(0\in f(\bar x)+Q(\bar x)\).
The mapping \(x\mapsto f(\bar x)+Df(\bar x)(x-\bar x)+Q(x)\) is strongly regular at \((\bar x,0)\).
For the quadratic rate, \(Df\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\to\bar x\) Q-superlinearly, and Q-quadratically when \(Df\) is locally Lipschitz.

notation.meaning: set-valued term in the generalized equation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Josephy iteration for a generalized equation with a fixed set-valued term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Josephy-Newton iterate \(x_{k+1}\) is the locally selected solution of \[0\in f(x_k)+Df(x_k)(x_{k+1}-x_k)+Q(x_{k+1}).\] Strong regularity makes this local solution single valued and Lipschitz in the linearization perturbation. Hence every sufficiently close \(x_0\) generates iterates converging to \(\bar x\), with \[\|x_{k+1}-\bar x\|=o(\|x_k-\bar x\|).\] If \(Df\) is locally Lipschitz, the estimate strengthens to \(\|x_{k+1}-\bar x\|=O(\|x_k-ar x\|^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong regularity of the generalized-equation linearization yields a locally unique Josephy step, superlinear convergence, and quadratic convergence under a Lipschitz derivative.
knowledge_statements.title: Josephy-Newton Convergence Family

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An exact Josephy-Newton convergence source is required to confirm that strong regularity of the frozen linearization and the stated differentiability assumptions yield the claimed local selection and rates. The quadratic estimate also contains the malformed expression \(x_k-ar x\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local convergence of the Josephy-Newton method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local superlinear convergence and Hölder-dependent convergence order under strong regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,Y\) be Banach spaces, let \(G:X\to Y\) be continuously Fréchet differentiable, and let \(N:X\rightrightarrows Y\) have closed graph. If \(\bar x\) is a strongly regular solution of \(0\in G(x)+N(x)\), then the Josephy-Newton method is locally \(q\)-superlinearly convergent to \(\bar x\). If, additionally, \(G'\) is \(\alpha\)-Hölder continuous near \(\bar x\), then the convergence order is \(1+\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuously Fréchet-differentiable generalized equation whose set-valued term has closed graph, strong regularity of a solution guarantees local q-superlinear convergence of the Josephy-Newton method. If the derivative is locally Hölder continuous with exponent α, the convergence order is 1+α.

children.title: Semismooth-Star Convergence Family
children.top_down_role: Local convergence for coderivative and subspace-based generalized-equation models.

assumptions_latex: \(G:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^n\) has \((\bar x,0)\in\operatorname{gph}G\) and is semismooth-star at \((\bar x,0)\).
The admissible coderivative or subspace models \(L_k\) are uniformly invertible, with inverse norms bounded by \(M\).
The chosen model satisfies \(\operatorname{dist}(0,G(x_k)+L_k s_k)=o(\|x_k-\bar x\|)\) and the semismooth-star model error is first-order vanishing.

notation.meaning: selected coderivative or subspace linear model

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract finite-dimensional coderivative/subspace Newton formulation; the exact semismooth-star variant requires certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_k\) be a step produced by an admissible semismooth-star coderivative or subspace model \(L_k\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\). If the selected models remain uniformly invertible and their combined equation residual and graph-linearization error are \(o(\|x_k-ar x\|)\), then every sufficiently close admissible sequence is well defined and satisfies \[\|x_{k+1}-\bar x\|\le M\,o(\|x_k-ar x\|)=o(\|x_k-ar x\|).\] Thus the local convergence is Q-superlinear.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Semismooth-star graph approximation and uniformly regular coderivative or subspace models imply local Q-superlinear convergence when model solves have vanishing relative error.
knowledge_statements.title: Semismooth-Star Convergence Family

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Semismooth-star Newton results depend on the precise graph, coderivative, or subspace model and its regularity assumptions. No source is supplied to identify the intended theorem, and several occurrences of \(x_k-ar x\) are malformed. The claimed convergence theorem therefore cannot be certified.

children.title: Inexact-Perturbed Local Convergence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Local behavior under inaccuracies in solves, derivatives, residuals, and parameters.

children.title: Inexact-Solve Rate Regimes
children.top_down_role: Rate preservation under controlled local-system solution errors.

assumptions_latex: The iteration error is \(e_k=x_k-\bar x\), and an exact local-model step \(s_k^*\) satisfies \(\|e_k+s_k^*\|\le C\|e_k\|^{1+\alpha}\), where \(C>0\) and \(0<\alpha\le 1\).
The computed step \(s_k\) satisfies \(\|s_k-s_k^*\|\le\eta_k\|e_k\|\), where \(\eta_k\ge 0\), and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|e_{k+1}\|\le C\|e_k\|^{1+\alpha}+\eta_k\|e_k\|\), with the preserved local rate determined by \(\eta_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic perturbation law for locally convergent Newton-type model solves.

source_refs.locator: 7.5.1 Linear Newton approximation schemes p. 703
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The exact-step and solve-error bounds imply \[\|e_{k+1}\|\le C\|e_k\|^{1+\alpha}+\eta_k\|e_k\|.\] If \(\eta_k\le\bar\eta<1\) for all sufficiently large \(k\), the recurrence gives local Q-linear convergence. If \(\eta_k\to0\), it gives Q-superlinear convergence. If \(\eta_k=O(\|e_k\|^\alpha)\), it preserves the exact local order \(1+\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniformly bounded relative solve error below one preserves linear convergence, a vanishing relative error gives superlinear convergence, and an order-matched error preserves the exact local order.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Solve Rate Regimes

children.title: Derivative-Approximation Rate Regimes
children.top_down_role: Local rate behavior for approximate, secant, and quasi-Newton derivative models.

assumptions_latex: The exact Newton model \(V_k\) is uniformly invertible and yields \(\|e_k-V_k^{-1}F(x_k)\|=O(\|e_k\|^{1+\alpha})\).
The approximate matrix \(B_k\) is invertible and the step is \(s_k=-B_k^{-1}F(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Dennis-Moré-type directional defect yields \(\|e_{k+1}\|=o(\|e_k\|)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional Dennis-Moré condition for approximate generalized derivatives.

source_refs.locator: 7.5.1 Linear Newton approximation schemes p. 703
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the steps satisfy \(B_k s_k=-F(x_k)\), \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\), and \(s_k=O(\|e_k\|)\). The approximate model preserves superlinear convergence when its error vanishes along the computed directions: \[\frac{\|(B_k-V_k)s_k\|}{\|s_k\|}\longrightarrow0.\] If instead \(\|(B_k-V_k)s_k\|=O(\|e_k\|^{1+\alpha})\), then the local order \(1+\alpha\) of the exact model is preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate derivatives preserve superlinear convergence when their errors vanish along computed steps; order-matched directional errors preserve the exact local order.
knowledge_statements.title: Derivative-Approximation Rate Regimes

children.title: Residual-Evaluation Error Regimes
children.top_down_role: Accuracy floors and rate degradation caused by inexact residual evaluations.

assumptions_latex: Let \(e_k=x_k-\bar x\). Using the exact residual in a fixed local Newton model produces an update satisfying \(\|e_{k+1}^{\mathrm{exact}}\|\le C\|e_k\|^{1+\alpha}\), where \(C>0\) and \(0<\alpha\le1\).
The evaluated residual is \(\widetilde F(x_k)=F(x_k)+\delta_k\), and the same model matrix \(V_k\) is used for the perturbed update, with \(\|V_k^{-1}\|\le M\).

notation.meaning: exact local convergence order minus one

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive residual noise under a uniformly stable local Newton model.

source_refs.locator: 7.5.1 Linear Newton approximation schemes p. 703
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Using \(\widetilde F(x_k)\) instead of \(F(x_k)\) in the same model adds the perturbation \(-V_k^{-1}\delta_k\), so \[\|e_{k+1}\|\le C\|e_k\|^{1+\alpha}+M\|\delta_k\|.\] The condition \(\|\delta_k\|=o(\|e_k\|)\) is sufficient to retain Q-superlinear convergence under this estimate, while \(\|\delta_k\|=O(\|e_k\|^{1+\alpha})\) preserves order \(1+\alpha\). A persistent bound \(\|\delta_k\|\le\varepsilon\) generally yields only an accuracy guarantee of order \(M\varepsilon\) in the local regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual noise is amplified by model inversion; sufficiently small relative noise preserves superlinear convergence, order-matched noise preserves the exact rate, and persistent noise produces an accuracy floor in the local estimate.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Evaluation Error Regimes

children.title: Parameter-Perturbation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Local tracking behavior for parameterized equation families.

assumptions_latex: \(0\in G(x,p)\) at \((\bar x,\bar p)\), and the generalized equation is strongly regular with respect to \(x\).
The associated local solution mapping \(s(p)\) is Lipschitz with modulus \(L\).
At stage \(k\), the local corrector contracts toward \(s(p_{k+1})\) with factor \(q_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strongly regular parameterized generalized equations with one local corrector per parameter change.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Strong regularity gives a locally single-valued solution branch satisfying \[\|s(p')-s(p)\|\le L\|p'-p\|.\] If one corrector at parameter \(p_{k+1}\) has contraction factor \(q_k\), then \[\|x_{k+1}-s(p_{k+1})\|\le q_k\bigl(\|x_k-s(p_k)\|+L\|p_{k+1}-p_k\|\bigr).\] Consequently, bounded \(q_k<1\) tracks sufficiently small parameter changes, while superlinear tracking requires both \(q_k\to0\) and parameter increments negligible relative to the current tracking error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong regularity creates a Lipschitz solution branch; tracking error combines the previous correction error with the size of the next parameter change.
knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Perturbation Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied for the strong-regularity tracking result or for the assumed one-step corrector contraction. Moreover, the final superlinear-tracking condition is not derived precisely: because the parameter increment is multiplied by \(q_k\), requiring it to be negligible relative to the current error is generally stronger than necessary. The intended specialized theorem must be sourced before revision.

children.title: Local Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural causes of undefined models, loss of fast convergence, cycling, or attraction to nonroots.

children.title: Generalized-Derivative Singularity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Rank loss or deteriorating inverse bounds in selected generalized derivatives.

children.title: Singular Generalized-Derivative Models
children.top_down_role: Selected generalized derivatives exhibiting rank loss near the solution.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generalized derivative at the root is singular, so an ordinary Newton equation cannot define a locally uniformly regular step.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar smooth example, hence also a nonsmooth generalized-derivative boundary case.

source_refs.locator: 9.1.4 Nonsingularity of Newton approximation p. 822
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=x^2\), the Bouligand and Clarke generalized derivatives coincide with the classical derivative: \(\partial_B F(x)=\partial F(x)=\{2x\}\). At the root, \[\partial F(0)=\{0\},\] so every available generalized-derivative model is singular. The Newton equation \(V s=-F(0)\) does not determine a unique step when \(V=0\), and no neighborhood of the root admits a uniform inverse bound for all selected models.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the equation x squared equals zero, the only generalized derivative at the root is zero, so uniform Newton-model invertibility fails.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular Generalized-Derivative Models

children.title: Unbounded-Inverse Generalized-Derivative Models
children.top_down_role: Selected generalized derivatives whose inverse bounds deteriorate locally.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Invertible derivative models approach singularity and have unbounded inverse norms as \(x_2\to0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth two-dimensional example isolating inverse-norm blow-up before singularity.

source_refs.locator: 9.1.4 Nonsingularity of Newton approximation p. 822
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At every point with \(x_2\ne0\), the derivative model is invertible and equals \[DF(x)=\operatorname{diag}(1,2x_2).\] Nevertheless, \(\sigma_{\min}(DF(x))=\min\{1,2|x_2|\}\), and therefore \[\|DF(x)^{-1}\|=\max\{1,(2|x_2|)^{-1}\}\longrightarrow\infty\quad\text{as }x_2\to0.\] Thus pointwise nonsingularity away from the root does not provide the uniform inverse bound needed for stable local Newton estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Derivative matrices can remain invertible at every nonroot iterate while their inverse norms diverge, destroying uniform stability near the root.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded-Inverse Generalized-Derivative Models
